item.title: England Records 5,258 Heat-Linked Deaths This Summer- Health Agency
item.description: England registered 5,258 deaths linked to this summer’s heat, the highest number of such fatalities on record, the UK’s Health Security Agency (UKHSA) said in estimates released Tuesday. “Summer 2026 was an exceptional summer, with the highest mortality observed since 2016, when the UKHSA began publishing annual heat mortality reports,” the agency said in a provisional report. Britain experienced its hottest summer on record this year, characterised by early and successive heatwaves. The country has also seen an exceptional drought that resulted from a lack of rainfall not seen in nearly 200 years. Scientists say human-driven climate change is amplifying extreme weather events, with Europe warming faster than the global average and heatwaves growing more frequent and severe. While the provisional figures may be revised, the mortality impact “exceeds that observed in any previous annual heat-associated mortality estimate”, the UKHSA added. People use emergency blankets to protect themselves from the heat as they arrive at the Olympic stadium for a concert of US singer Bruno Mars on June 28, 2026, in Berlin. (Photo by RALF HIRSCHBERGER / AFP) The latest figure, logged across seven “heat episodes” between May and September, topples the previous record of 2,985 estimated heat-linked deaths in summer 2022. The UKHSA analysis compares mortality during periods of heat with mortality during “nearby non-heat periods”, the agency said. This is particularly useful for understanding the impacts of heatwaves, it added. Multiple European countries registered record heat-related deaths after a sweltering summer this year, including Germany with 16,300 and more than 5,000 in Spain. A report published in The Lancet medical journal last month said climate change must be declared a “global health emergency” and found there were more than three million deaths caused by heat between 2016 and 2023. Tourists shield themselves from the sun with umbrellas at St Peter’s Square in the Vatican during a heatwave, on June 24, 2026. (Photo by Filippo MONTEFORTE / AFP) Heat-related excess deaths often result from the higher risk of heart attacks and strokes caused by the strain of trying to keep body temperatures stable. Britain’s national weather agency has predicted the El Nino weather pattern could make 2027 the hottest year globally. Experts are urging the country to better prepare homes and public infrastructure for warmer summers. AFP The post England Records 5,258 Heat-Linked Deaths This Summer- Health Agency appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Freshman phenom Tim Ibukunoluwa off to historic start for Siena
item.description: Siena's Tim Ibukunoluwa (13) drives past St. John's Reed Bailey (13) during the first half of an NCAA college basketball game Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026, in the Queens borough of New York. (AP Photo/Frank Franklin II) (Frank Franklin II/Associated Press) ALBANY - Only six games into his college basketball career, Siena freshman Tim Ibukunoluwa is making Metro Conference history. He was named Metro Player and Rookie of the Week on Monday for the third time in as many weeks to begin the season. He's the first Metro freshman to win three Player of the Week honors in an entire season in the 47-year history of the league. "I kind of just try not to look at it," Ibukunoluwa said before practice. "I know what my goal is. My goal is to win every single game, win the Metro and get to the tournament. That (awards) stuff isn't really any of my goals, but obviously, it's nice for it to come with it. So I'm just looking at the wins." Siena fans will get to see the 6-foot-8 Australian phenom in person again when the Saints take on the University of Vermont at 7 p.m. Tuesday at MVP Arena. He's tied for fourth in the country at 25.2 points per game and ranks ninth at 10.5 rebounds per contest. In Saturday's 93-87 win at Bucknell , Ibukunoluwa finished with 34 points, 15 rebounds and six assists to become the first Division I freshman with at least 30 points, 15 rebounds and five assists in a game since the 1938-39 season, when the NCAA Tournament began, according to the data sites CBB Analytics and Stathead. He's the first Metro player in any class to win three straight Player of the Week awards since Iona's Nelly Junior Joseph won four in a row from Dec. 12, 2022 to Jan. 2, 2023. "He's been awesome with (the attention)," Siena coach Nevada Smith said. "He understands it. He's such a team-first guy. He just cares about winning and that's been his whole thing the whole time. He's just doing what it takes to help our team win and whatever comes to him is definitely well-deserved, but he's handled it really well." Ibukunoluwa also scored 16 points in last Wednesday's loss at St. John's. Red Storm coaching legend Rick Pitino said after that game that Ibukunoluwa has "great potential" and should stay at Siena as a sophomore to develop rather than transferring to a higher-level program for more money. Ibukunoluwa said he and his family haven't mapped out a long-term plan. "They just want the best for me and I want the best for myself," Ibukunoluwa said. "Just staying at a school that's going to have good development, that's going to push me and just to play somewhere I'm very comfortable and that I'm always trying to work and improve myself." Asked if he's worried about bigger schools trying to tamper with Ibukunoluwa, Smith replied, "Oh, for sure, they already try." "It's the worst thing about having a really good player at our level," Smith said. item.title: Texas football hit a home run with free agent LBs Raheem Biles, Justin Cryer | Golden
item.description: Texas Longhorns head coach Steve Sarkisian and linebacker Justin Cryer (28) embrace during senior day celebrations ahead of the Longhorns' 45-3 win over the Arkansas Razorbacks at Royal-Memorial Stadium in Austin, Nov. 21, 2026. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman) It's never enough for true hunters. Justin Cryer and Raheem Biles embody that way of doing business. As a result, the Texas Longhorns are in nice position to do some great over the next month or so. When they take to the road for Friday's regular-season finale at Texas A&M, it will be with the accepted obligation that the defense will lead this team wherever it might be going, be it the SEC championship game, the College Football Playoff or both. Take a look at the two rosters that will go at it Friday and the Longhorns get the edge over the Aggies in the area of free-agent pickups, especially the two star linebackers. Yeah, I know it sounds like college football has become very NFL-like when it comes to acquiring talent that didn't come via the high school route. Texas Longhorns head coach Steve Sarkisian greets linebacker Rasheem Biles (3) during senior day celebrations ahead of the Longhorns' 45-3 win over the Arkansas Razorbacks at Royal-Memorial Stadium in Austin, Nov. 21, 2026. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman) MORE CEDDY: Texas should crush Texas A&M but never assume The Longhorns are a top-five team that's locked up a CFP spot and has a chance to play in the final SEC championship game in large part because of some name free agents. UP NEXT NO. 5 TEXAS VS. TEXAS A&M When/where: 6:30 p.m. Friday in College Station. TV/radio: ABC; 1300 AM, 1370 AM, 98.5 FM, 105.3 FM (Spanish). Biles and Cryer have brought some great leadership to a defense that wasn't lacking in that department with established vets like defensive tackle Hero Kanu, edge rusher Colin Simmons and safety Jelani McDonald already in place. If someone from Mars landed Sunday and was invited to Texas' regular Monday news conference, they would come away believing Biles and Cryer have been part of the Texas program for years because of the experience they brought with them. Coach Steve Sarkisian said he needed maturity in the locker room, which made Biles and Cryer ideal transfer candidates once he vetted them. "We lost some older players that had moved on, and we knew we had a really good group of young players coming in," Sarkisian said. "How could we get some maturity? Coach (Will) Muschamp's defense is not simple and a lot gets put on the 'backers to do multiple things. And so, to have a level of maturity and have a have a real sense and a real football IQ about them, allows them to come in and then kind of springboard with the scheme to go take it and go run with it. Those were two critical factors that I thought both those guys checked the boxes for us." item.title: 18 brilliant and surprising gifts for science lovers this Christmas
item.description: This moon lamp is a hot Christmas tip from designer Phoebe Watts (see below) Gingko Design The New Scientist Christmas gift guide is assembled by our crack team of science editors and experts. If you’re struggling for gift ideas, you will find unexpected and ingenious suggestions for amateur astronomers and animal and nature lovers, as well as those fond of food, beauty and puzzles. And surely that covers all of us? Space reporter Leah Crane recommends the science-themed jigsaws from Nervous System Nervous System Puzzlingly beautiful: a science jigsaw If you’re looking for a quick and easy jigsaw to breeze through while watching holiday movies, Nervous System puzzles probably aren’t for you. But if you want something that’s part puzzle, part work of art, and that will keep you transfixed for hours, they’ll definitely do the trick. Nervous System makes laser-cut wooden puzzles with uniquely shaped pieces and science themes, and they are absolutely beautiful. I’m particularly a fan of their geode puzzles, featuring concentric wiggles of bright colour, including wiggly sides that defy every puzzler’s instinct to start with the edge pieces. For even more of a challenge, they make infinity puzzles that can be assembled and reassembled many different ways – those have no edge pieces at all, and some don’t even have a picture on them! Nervous System also sells absolutely stunning jewellery, lamps and sculptures, but to me the puzzles are the real show-stoppers. Nervous System puzzles , from $45 (£32) Advertisement Leah Crane The CL Companion 8×30 binoculars, as recommended by senior editor Chelsea Whyte Swarovski Optik Zoom in: splashing out on binoculars The eccentric filmmaker Werner Herzog famously declared that he travels with only a second set of underwear, a map, a toothbrush and a set of binoculars. I don’t travel quite so lightly, but on my next trip, I definitely want to add a pair of nice binos to my baggage. I tested out three sets at varying price levels, taking them down to my favourite spot on my local river and out to my backyard during a clear night with a half-moon overhead. The Nikon Prostaff P3 8×42 binoculars are extremely well balanced and were the most comfortable in my hands. They were particularly well-suited for twilight and brighter. The other Nikon set I tried was the Stabilised 12×25 S, which is much more compact. For my small hands that was fine, and the stabilisation was marvellous at reducing any shaking, both while looking at something fixed like the moon or moving quickly to track an eagle fishing for dinner. The stabilisation requires batteries, so these are probably best – suited to the more prepared adventurer. The stand – out pair was the CL Companion 8×30 from Swarovski Optik. I’ve never seen anything look better than they did through these lenses. They let in an enormous amount of light, making the world look like the brightness has been turned up. And the moon’s craters looked stunningly crisp. For the birdwatcher

item.title: How weird vibes from the Springboks could have huge impact in Nations Championship final
item.description: To whatever extent the words of Rassie Erasmus were lost in translation last week, South Africa used their team announcement press conference on Monday to make a clear point. With Erasmus unable to conduct media duties under the terms of his ban from World Rugby , assistant coach Mzwandile Stick stood in at the Springboks ’ hotel in southwest London – taking questions in English but answering only in Xhosa, his first language. It was explained that the coaching staff wanted to ensure nothing was misinterpreted. With the dedicated Kuhle Sonkosi – a former lock who now works for South African broadcaster SuperSport – acting as an impromptu translator, Stick spent a slightly stilted half-an-hour explaining a heavily-changed team for the Nations Championship final against France. He espoused the virtues of Manu Tshituka, the Congo-born back rower compared to Pieter-Steph du Toit primed for an international debut at Twickenham on Sunday. Mzwandile Stick conducted his press briefing entirely in Xhosa (PA) At one point, Stick cracked a joke about his good looks being the reason he attracted more attention than other coaches from the cameras in Dublin, insisting that it had been a collective effort to replace Erasmus. To Sonkosi’s credit, the remark drew a chuckle even on translation. Clearly, the coach was entitled to converse in his mother tongue if he wished to; South Africa has 12 official languages, of course. As is generally the case, he was engaging company. Stick (left) stood in for Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus (Getty) Yet one could should not shake a slightly peculiar feel. In part, that has to do with a side going into a final, with two trophies potentially on the line, on the heels of consecutive defeats. “Obviously, it’s not ideal to go into the final having lost back-to-back losses,” Stick admitted. “I think the more we’re frustrated at is that we haven’t played to our standards. For us, it’s very important to stop this run.” A shot at revenge against France is welcome after a game of fine margins; the Springboks coach rightly noted that his side had come out on the right side of three one-point contests on their way to World Cup glory two years ago. But the weirdness pervaded beyond the oddities of this new competition. Just a quarter-of-an-hour before Stick sat down to speak, Erasmus was posting on social media not about the team about to be named, or the Springboks nominated for World Rugby awards, but about his plans to once again livestream his reaction on Sunday afternoon. “Watchwithrassie” had proved a success of sorts , with more than 100,000 people in South Africa signing up to watch a silent stream of the South African supremo sat on his own in a hotel room and occasionally appearing to speak into his phone. “Sound will remain off until Rassie wants to speak,” a chyron said – the unmute button was never pressed. item.title: Jaime Jaquez Jr. Still Fits Miami Heat Culture Despite Trade
item.description: Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images The trade sent Jaime Jaquez Jr. to Milwaukee, yet the Miami Heat connection never truly broke. He returned to the Kaseya Center on November 18 wearing a Bucks jersey and played with the same grit Miami fans love. With the Heat securing a 137–130 victory, he tallied 10 points and dished out five assists to lead his team in that matchup. According to local reports from Ethan Skolnick, insiders and fans are already anticipating a potential reunion as soon as he becomes available. Jaquez has not lost his edge in his first 18 games with the Bucks. He is averaging 14.6 points, 4.8 rebounds, and 2.9 assists while shooting 42.5% from three-point range. Yahoo Sports notes that his performance has cemented the view that he personifies the traits characterizing “Heat culture.” This culture relies on physicality, downhill pressure, and a willingness to do the dirty work without needing special plays drawn up. Why The Heat Still Want Him Back Miami values players who fit their specific identity, and Jaquez fits it perfectly. His blue-collar mentality matches the ethos the franchise demands from every single player on the roster. Although the Bucks hold the reins on his restricted free agency and any extension discussions, the connection between his style and Miami’s requirements persists. The front office knows that a player who works hard and plays tough is exactly what they need to win again. Fans will keep watching his progress closely as the season unfolds. Should the trade market change, they seek an opportunity to bring him back to South Florida. His stats show he can score and defend, which are the two most important things for a Heat forward. A Look At The Current Roster The Heat are also finding their own rhythm with other young players. Nikola Jovic is carving out a role thanks to his defensive tenacity, though his shooting splits are still low at 32.4/25.0/78.6. Meanwhile, Davion Mitchell has become a key piece after joining in the Jimmy Butler trade. He is averaging 17 points and 8.6 assists while shooting 51% from the field. Mitchell’s ascent has aided the Heat throughout their ongoing seven-game winning streak. Dwyane Wade praised his work ethic on his YouTube channel, noting that Mitchell travels with a basketball everywhere he goes as a grown man. “A guy that walks around and travel with a basketball everywhere he goes as a grown man, I’m rocking with him,” said Wade. The Heat have a clear path forward with players who love the game and work hard. Whether Jaquez returns or not, the team has found a way to keep its core values alive. The roster is built on players who understand what it takes to succeed in Miami. Jaquez recorded 10 points and five assists in his return game on November 18.

item.title: Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana hits out at Real Madrid star Kylian Mbappe critics and demands respect for 'killer' former PSG superstar
item.description: Kylian Mbappe - Getty Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana has mounted a passionate defence of Kylian Mbappe's Ligue 1 record, insisting his international team-mate's achievements are far too often downplayed. The French centre-back also sparked debate by comparing Mbappe at his peak to Brazilian icon Neymar. Fofana leaps to defence of Mbappe's French legacy Fofana has passionately defended Mbappe's record in Ligue 1, arguing that the forward's achievements in France are frequently trivialised. Speaking as a guest on the YouTube show Zack en Roue Libre , the French centre-back insisted that critics fail to appreciate the true scale of Mbappe's dominance during his time in his homeland. Mbappe rose through the youth academy at Monaco before spending seven prolific years at PSG. Despite his extraordinary goalscoring output across those seasons, Fofana believes public perception has unfairly downplayed his domestic exploits. Chelsea star compares prime Mbappe to Neymar To illustrate Mbappe's brilliance, Fofana weighed the French superstar against his former PSG star Neymar, placing the Brazilian just behind football's two greatest modern icons. However, the Chelsea defender maintained that Mbappe's relentless efficiency in Ligue 1 matched Neymar's peak level. "If you take Mbappe in his prime and Neymar in his prime, it is a close contest," Fofana said. "Neymar is the ultimate player after CR7 and Messi. But what I saw from Mbappe in Ligue 1 was insane. We trivialise what he did far too much." A dominant seven-year spell in the French capital After bursting onto the scene with Monaco, Mbappe seven-year stint at PSG saw him deliver relentless consistency week after week in Ligue 1. Having faced the challenge of defending against top-level attackers himself, Fofana offered a player's perspective on how difficult it is to maintain that standard. By labelling Mbappe a "hitman", the Chelsea defender emphasised the ruthless predictability of his goalscoring rather than sheer spectacle. "Mbappe is a hitman; every weekend it's a goal," he noted. "With Neymar, there is the flair, the madness, because you tell yourself, 'imagine if he had been serious'." Debate continues over Mbappe's place among football's elite Fofana's candid assessment is sure to fuel ongoing debates among supporters regarding how Mbappe's years in France should be judged alongside his peers. What is certain is that Mbappe will continue his campaign with Real Madrid this season, with Los Blancos set to face PSV in the Champions League. Meanwhile, Fofana will look to help the Blues secure a victory as they travel to face Nottingham Forest in the Premier League this weekend.

item.title: Liverpool have set their sights on move for 17-year-old midfielder
item.description: Liverpool have set their sights on move for 17-year-old midfielder Liverpool Eye Abdellah Ouazane as Julian Ward Steps Up Florian Wirtz Support Plan Liverpool are advancing plans in the market again, with fresh attention turning towards Ajax teenager Abdellah Ouazane as the club shapes the next phase of its squad build under Andoni Iraola and Julian Ward. According to Anfield Watch, the thinking at Anfield is increasingly focused on depth behind Florian Wirtz, whose recent form has underlined both his importance and the need for smart cover. The original report states that Liverpool are “exploring moves to sign a back-up for the German international” and that the club are now “ramping up moves to sign a back-up for Wirtz in the January window”. IMAGO Florian Wirtz Form Driving Liverpool Planning There is a straightforward logic to this. Liverpool are pleased with Wirtz and the numbers support that stance. As reported, he “created 10 chances against Man United all by himself” and now has “four assists and six goals in his last nine starts for club and country”. Those returns offer a strong indication of why he remains central to the attacking structure. Internally, there appears to be an acceptance that elite talent still needs protection. The report says Ward and the recruitment staff “are well aware that Wirtz needs a deputy. Liverpool cannot rely on him alone.” That line feels important. Recruitment at top clubs is rarely about replacing quality already in the building, it is about insulating it, sustaining it and ensuring the level does not drop across a long season. Abdellah Ouazane Emerges on Liverpool Shortlist Among the names under consideration, Ouazane stands out. Anfield Watch reports that “the Moroccan attacking midfielder who plays for Ajax has also been looked at by the Reds and is a serious candidate.” For Liverpool, that profile makes immediate sense. Ouazane is described as a player with versatility and projection. He has operated from the left, though he is also characterised as “a traditional no.10” and someone who “has also been deployed as a no.8 at youth level”. That positional flexibility has become increasingly valuable in modern recruitment, especially for clubs looking to future-proof several roles with one signing. The background is compelling too. He has “already represented Morocco at senior international level despite being only 17-years-old” and is “regarded as one of the best Ajax prospects to have come through the club’s prestigious academy in the last decade”. Those are significant endorsements for a player still at the beginning of his career. Ajax Talent Fits Long-Term Liverpool Strategy Liverpool’s wider strategy appears clear. This is a club trying to collect elite young talent before the market fully inflates around them. The report frames it in ambitious terms, saying, “Signing him would change everything for Liverpool.” That is expansive language, but the broader point is understandable. Ouazane is part of

item.title: Aneurin Donald and Phil Salt demolish Australia as England level T20 series
item.description: England’s all-Welsh opening partnership of Aneurin Donald and Phil Salt annihilated Australia with a brutal display of power hitting to level the T20 series in style on the Gold Coast. The pair rained down 13 sixes on the Carrara Oval in a frenzied stand of 151 that saw them make a target of 185 look like child’s play, speeding to an eight-wicket thrashing with 6.5 overs unused. The silent partner of the England and Wales Cricket Board made itself known in no uncertain terms after a false start in Melbourne on Saturday, with Swansea-born Donald blitzing 85 in 32 balls and Salt – who traded Denbighshire for Barbados as a schoolboy – adding 58 off 30. It was a devastating display which left some nasty scars on a pieced-together Australia attack that performed impressively to go 1-0 ahead at the MCG. Nikhil Chaudhary was taken apart by Donald in the fifth over, leaking 26 runs, before left-armer Joel Davies suffered even more grievously at Salt’s hands. Phil Salt batting for England on the Gold Coast (Dave Hunt/AAPImage via AP) His second over disappeared for an excruciating 31, including four sixes, a boundary and three skittish wides as he tried to hide the ball from his tormentor. Donald was hurtling towards a century when he picked out the catcher at long-on but, having scored just 56 runs in his first four innings during an uncertain start to his international career, this was no time for regrets. Salt also fell before the end, courtesy of a brilliant one-handed caught-and-bowled by Ben Dwarshuis, but their bullying partnership meant that was little more than damage-limitation. Tom Banton finished it off from the first ball of the 13th over, clearing the ropes for the third time in his own eight-ball cameo to end Australia’s pain. Despite the dominant nature of the chase, Australia would have been relatively content at the changeover, carving out 184 for eight on an unpredictable drop-in pitch. It turned out to be nowhere near enough but, after nailing 50 off the last three overs and watching Ben Dwarshuis end the innings with three consecutive sixes off Sam Curran , they had made their charge. England began by handing a debut to James Coles, who was immediately tasked with the first over of the day. He settled quickly by allowing just five singles, but that was a calm moment in an otherwise manic powerplay, during which Australia swung their way to 58 at the cost of four wickets. Henry Crocombe took this catch to dismiss Mitch Marsh (Dave Hunt/AP) Captain Mitch Marsh set the tone, flogging Henry Crocombe for two off-side sixes which sailed into the stands then popping a return catch back to the seamer as he tightened up his line under pressure. Jake Fraser-McGurk was reading from the same all-or-nothing playbook, at one stage clearing the ropes three times in five balls – including two big hits off Coles’ second visit. item.title: “Your Job to Create That Environment”: Fans Blame Lane Kiffin as He Criticizes Players for Playing for Themselves Ahead of Bowl Games
item.description: Louisiana State Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin. © Reuters LSU’s chances of making the college football playoffs are done and dusted, and with pressure on Lane Kiffin to justify the huge price tag that came with his appointment, the head coach would want his team to end on a high with the bowl games coming up. But Kiffin believes that players are only playing for themselves in the NIL era, pointing out the challenges that come with this generation. “They’re going to play for themselves and so if they put out bad film, they make bad decisions, they don’t hustle on a play, or they don’t play well, they’re hurting themselves whether that’s here or whether that’s somewhere else next year when they go to negotiate,” he said. Kiffin’s comments weren’t necessarily echoed by fans, with one saying, “He’s going to need a lot of talent to win with this attitude, it’s your job to create that environment in this landscape of college football it’s not easy for reasons he stated but you got to find that or LSU is going to have a budget bigger than anyone else and by a good margin.” Lane Kiffin Apologized for Using Profanity in a Halftime Interview Lane Kiffin recently used some foul language at halftime on LSU’s radio network during the game against Tennessee, and was quick to apologize for his comments after LSU’s safety Ty Benefield was ejected for targeting. “I want to apologize for my language at halftime in the interview,” Kiffin said to reporters. “No excuses. I was frustrated with the first half and really couldn’t even hear the question, kind of like our center down in the student section. But there’s no reason for that. And so, to people who were offended, I apologize for that.” Kiffin also pointed out one core issue he wants to address with this LSU team. “I keep saying, ‘I’m not concerned about the future of the program. I’m excited about the future of the program, but we have one core issue to fix, and that’s how we finish games. We’re in these games against really, really good teams, and we don’t play well late, and that can be part of a mindset that we don’t have right.” LSU plays Arkansas this Saturday in Fayetteville. item.title: Red Sox Face Intriguing Triston Casas Question Following Offseason Roster Changes

Much of the attention surrounding the Boston Red Sox this offseason has focused on their recent acquisitions and the uncertainty involving outfielder Jarren Duran. item.title: Roma eyeing Sporting Lisbon forward Fotis Ioannidis
item.description: Roma eyeing Sporting Lisbon forward Fotis Ioannidis Roma continues to monitor the attacking market ahead of the winter transfer window, evaluating various opportunities to strengthen Gian Piero Gasperini’s attack. Following rumors of interest in Endrick, another name has emerged that could fuel competition with AC Milan: Fotis Ioannidis, a 2000-born Greek striker currently playing for Sporting CP. AC Milan is closely monitoring Ioannidis in their search for a centre-forward to replace Camarda, including the Greek among the options being evaluated along with Endrick and Tresoldi. One potential player who could influence AC Milan’s interest is Ruben Amorim, who has previously worked with the striker at Sporting CP and knows his characteristics. According to Gianluca Di Marzio, Roma considers the player an interesting prospect, although they haven’t identified him as a top priority. The European calendar will soon offer the Giallorossi the opportunity to observe the striker firsthand. On December 8th, Ioannidis will face Roma in the Champions League for Sporting CP, a match that could be an important opportunity to assess his qualities. So far, the Greek has made 15 appearances this season, scoring two goals and providing two assists. Gasperini, however, is primarily looking for a winger with acceleration, the ability to beat his man, and the ability to attack space—characteristics different from those of a central striker like the Greek. Therefore, any further exploration of Ioannidis will also depend on the opportunities that arise during the January transfer window.

item.title: Kentucky Wildcat News: Mark Pope Hot Seat Talk
item.description: Good morning BBN! We are in the midst of a week off for the Kentucky Wildcats as they are coming off a loss to Indiana in Indianapolis. Now, the Cats are getting prepared for a matchup with the Wichita State Shockers in Rupp Arena on Friday night. However, the vibes among BBN and the national landscape are not great. That is where the “hot seat” talk is really starting to heat up. In all reality, it absolutely should. Things have not been up to the Kentucky Basketball standard for quite some time, and now it appears the program is about to hit rock bottom. The Cats have no juice, and the momentum for the season seems to be obsolete, meaning it feels like a breakup is more likely than not. Now, can the Cats turn it around? Absolutely, and all of us would likely jump for joy immediately during that period. That doesn’t change the momentum of this whole situation, though. Recruiting has been a struggle, and power conference games have been a pain to watch about 50% of the time. It just hasn’t been the standard. The hot seat talk is real and very valid. Now we just see how long it goes. item.title: Real Madrid superstar coming to terms with his new reality at the club – report
item.description: Real Madrid superstar coming to terms with his new reality at the club – report Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho has confirmed that Vinicius Jr. will start tonight against PSV Eindhoven, but the past month has done a lot of damage to the player’s status at the club. Serving a long suspension from La Liga for a red card he picked up against Villarreal, the Brazilian star slowly saw his place being taken over by Yan Diomande, whom the manager slowly began viewing as an option on the left flank. With the team’s results also improving after the forced change, it slowly began to become clear that Vinicius was no longer as irreplaceable as he had been over the years. For the first time in years, his place in the starting XI began being called into question. Phase of acceptance As reported by Radio Estadio Noche in a recent update, Vinicius is beginning to come to terms with the new reality around his situation. Diomande is slowly replacing Vinicius. (Photo by Milos Bicanski/Getty Images) He accepts that he is no longer an undisputed starter for Real Madrid, and that he can now be replaced in the dynamics. Needless to say, that requires a massive shift in mentality and a real sense of maturity for a player who has been the face of the club for years. With the acceptance of his situation, Vinicius also now understands that he may have to sit on the bench and watch Diomande as a starter for Real Madrid. Regardless of how mature his understanding may be, it will undoubtedly prick the player to see his spot being owned by a teammate. A hope for resurgence Vinicius had a great international break. (Photo by Ryan Pierse/Getty Images) For a long time, Vinicius’ situation this season seemed hopeless and his arc appeared to only be moving downhill. The recent international break, however, provided a sense of hope for the first time and handed the player a major confidence boost. In Brazil’s two games in the recent hiatus, Vinicius scored five goals including a hat-trick and a brace, putting aside his poor form and rediscovering his goalscoring boots. He started on the bench at the weekend, but his cameo was powerful and even played a critical part in Real Madrid’s comeback. As he prepares to start tonight, the player will be aware that a lot rides on what he makes of the opportunity . After all, he is already treading on a tightrope and is a couple of poor performances from definitely losing his starting spot.

item.title: 2027 NFL mock draft after Week 11: Consensus picks for top 10
item.description: Another week of NFL action is in the books, and we have separated the contenders from the pretenders. Three teams are battling it out for the top pick in the 2027 NFL Draft at 1-9, but it’s the Tennessee Titans who currently lead the Jeremiah Smith sweepstakes. Over the next few weeks, we will be looking at the consensus top 10 picks across the web to determine who the top draft picks to keep an eye on are. We know that the Ohio State Buckeyes superstar will be one of the first few players off the board, likely No. 1 overall, but who will follow? The 2027 NFL Draft will be held from Thursday, April 29, through Saturday, May 1, at the National Mall outside of the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C. What are the experts saying about the direction your favorite team could go when they are on the clock? Let’s take a look at the current consensus picks for the 2027 NFL draft . The Ohio State superstar is undeniably the best offensive player in this year’s class and is a true difference maker. In eight games this season, Simmons has recorded 16 tackles for a loss and 10.5 sacks, highlighting just how disruptive he can be. The Chargers could go in several different directions, but for now, he is the pick in 56 percent of mocks. 3. item.title: Riding a 5–1 High Into Paris: Can Gasperini’s Roma Ambush a Depleted PSG?
item.description: Riding a 5–1 High Into Paris: Can Gasperini’s Roma Ambush a Depleted PSG? There’s nothing like a little canapé to tempt the palate, and four goals at the Stadio Ennio Tardini are just that: a great way of sharpening the appetite before a meeting of the heavyweights. With Donyell Malen achieving AS Roma’s first four-goal Serie A appearance since Vincenzo Montella in 2002 – and let’s not forget Rodrigo Mora’s stunning 71’ cherry on top of the cake – there’s a huge amount of momentum under the team’s feet. Now, the Giallorossi carry that momentum to the Parc des Princes on Wednesday for a pivotal Matchday 5 UEFA Champions League clash against two-time defending champions (and daunting foe) Paris Saint-Germain. While Luis Enrique faces his former club amid a 12-match winning streak across all competitions, PSG’s attack has been rocked by consecutive ACL ruptures to Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Désiré Doué . There’s a clear opening, and a huge amount of wind in the sails. So, is this the best time to strike? The Stakes in Paris Paris Saint-Germain sit at the top of the league table the 36-team standings at 4–0–0 with 12 points and a +15 goal differential, having piled up 20 goals while conceding five in victories over Barcelona, Manchester City, Villarreal, and Slovan Bratislava. Roma, however, occupy 20th place on four points (1–1–2, +2 goal differential) after falling 3–2 at Manchester United on Matchday 4. There’s a narrative that, taken at face value, doesn’t seem all that promising – tactical dominance vs a desperate fight for survival. And fans are acutely aware that, with only four league-phase fixtures remaining (and a home tie against Sporting CP next on December 8) the margin for error around the top-24 playoff cutoff is shrinking very quickly. Stealing points from the tournament’s pace-setters in Paris would give Gasperini’s squad invaluable cushion heading into winter. Fortunately for Roma, PSG’s double injury blow changes things a lot. Losing both Kvaratskhelia and Doué means that Luis Enrique’s left side has been stripped of vital press-breakers, creating an invitation for Gasperini’s trademark man-oriented pressing. If midfielders Manu Koné and Bryan Cristante can disrupt Vitinha and Fabián Ruiz early, aggressive wing-back overlaps from Molina and Wesley can pin back PSG’s full-backs and overload the channels. Still, surviving the Parc des Princes requires discipline. PSG average 5.0 goals and 57 percent possession per Champions League match, meaning Roma’s back three and in-form goalkeeper Mile Svilar must withstand sustained early pressure. Is This a Game for the Ages? Possibly, and recent history shows how one night can redraw the sport. We all remember PSG’s 5-0 win over Inter in the 2025 Champions League final, which won the club its first European title. More recently, the 2026 World Cup turned on a single moment, too. item.title: Video: ‘I’m going to be better CEO’ – Huang speaks after reinstatement as Nvidia boss
item.description: By Wasiu Rokibat Employees of American technology giant Nvidia have given Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang a rousing welcome as he returned to the company’s headquarters in Santa Clara, California, following his reinstatement. Huang received loud cheers, applause and chants from excited staff members when he arrived at the office on Monday, November 23, 2026. Addressing the cheering employees, the technology executive expressed appreciation for their support and acknowledged the opportunity to resume his leadership position. HILARIOUS: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on his first day back after being reinstated: “This is my first day of work. I don't have a computer, so the IT department is going to give me a new PC. I'm hoping it's an RTX Spark.” “I want to thank all of you. I'm terribly sorry for putting… — RedWave Press (@RedWavePress) November 23, 2026 “Thank you all for the second chance. I’m going to be a better CEO the second time around,” Huang told the gathering. His remarks were greeted with more applause as employees enthusiastically chanted his name. The dramatic return came after Nvidia’s board of directors unanimously voted to reinstate Huang as president and CEO, reversing his earlier departure from the company. Huang had stepped down on November 12 amid controversy surrounding allegations about his personal relationships and concerns involving a suspected foreign intelligence operation. The allegations have attracted considerable public and political attention. His reinstatement has also generated reactions beyond the company, with questions raised about corporate accountability, leadership and the influence of powerful executives in the technology industry. Meanwhile, the emotional reception from employees suggests that Huang still enjoys considerable support within parts of the company’s workforce. Nvidia, one of the world’s leading technology companies, plays a major role in the development of artificial intelligence through its advanced computer chips. item.title: Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana reveals Karim Benzema Champions League nightmare and admits he almost quit football
item.description: Chelsea FC v Manchester United - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana has opened up on the psychological toll of facing Real Madrid’s elite and the physical battles that nearly drove him out of the game entirely. The Frenchman described a specific Champions League encounter that left him feeling outclassed by the legendary Karim Benzema. Fofana opens up on brutal Bernabeu night Fofana has offered a stark assessment of his experiences facing the world's best, admitting that former Real Madrid captain Benzema left a lasting scar on his professional psyche. Reflecting on Chelsea’s 2023 Champions League quarter-final exit against the Spanish giants, the centre-back confessed to being overwhelmed by the sheer quality on display at the Santiago Bernabeu. The Blues lost both legs 2-0, with Benzema finding the net in the first encounter to set the tone for a dominant Madrid performance. "Benzema traumatised me. He took us out all by himself. Him and Vinícius, it was just nonsense. Rodrygo, he came to finish the job, because I'm not driven by goals. If we talk about football, the two of them, Vinícius and Benzema, it was too much, it was nonsense. We played against Modrić, they had a dream team,” Fofana revealed during an appearance on the YouTube show Zack , as quoted by Foot Mercato . The defender compares England's top flight to Europe The 25-year-old defender was quick to point out that while competing in England’s top flight demands an elite standard, stepping onto Europe’s biggest stage is a different beast altogether. Even with the prestige of representing a heavyweight like Chelsea, he admitted that facing continental royalty at the Santiago Bernabeu served as a stark reality check. "We went to play at the Santiago Bernabeu and they gave us a football lesson. Chelsea is a high level. You're in a big club, the Premier League is a high level, you're in a big league. But the Champions League is even higher. It’s higher still," Fofana added. The brink of early retirement Beyond the challenges on the pitch, Fofana’s time in West London has been heavily disrupted by a series of long-term fitness issues. The Frenchman has missed a staggering 696 days of action due to various ailments since moving to Stamford Bridge, including a significant ACL injury that sidelined him for nearly a year. These recurring setbacks eventually led him to a dark place where he seriously considered tearing up his contract and walking away from professional football for good. The defender reached a breaking point during the 2024-25 season while working under manager Enzo Maresca. After recovering from major knee surgery, he suffered consecutive thigh injuries that made him feel as though his body was fundamentally broken. "There was a period, when I came back from the ACL and meniscus injuries, I injured my thigh twice under Maresca. A period where I wanted to quit football," Fofana revealed. item.title: 'Create a dynasty!' - Bruno Guimaraes reveals Mikel Arteta's bold message and warns Arsenal rivals he has another level to reach
item.description: Newcastle United v Arsenal FC - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Bruno Guimaraes revealed Mikel Arteta immediately challenged him to help create a dynasty at Arsenal when he arrived from Newcastle United this summer. Ahead of Tuesday's Champions League clash with Borussia Dortmund, the Brazilian midfielder insisted he still has another level to reach alongside Declan Rice and Martin Odegaard. Guimaraes reveals Arteta's dynasty message Bruno Guimaraes has helped propel Arsenal to the top of the Premier League and an unbeaten Champions League league phase since arriving from Newcastle United this summer, yet he insists the best is still to come. Speaking to the media on Monday ahead of Tuesday night's meeting with Borussia Dortmund at Emirates Stadium, the Brazilian shared the ambitious mandate Mikel Arteta gave him upon signing . "We want to make a dynasty here; we want to win everything possible," Guimaraes said. "I think since I came to the club, the first thing Mikel said to me was create a dynasty for the club, so we want to win everything that's possible." Adapting to a freer role in midfield Despite scoring twice early in his Arsenal career and becoming an instant favourite with supporters, Guimaraes explained that adjusting to Arteta's fluid midfield demands has pushed him harder than ever. Playing across the number six, eight and nine spaces requires constant movement, and he leans heavily on Declan Rice and Martin Odegaard to sharpen his positioning. "It's very different, here is a little bit more free. You play as a six, an eight, and a nine sometimes, so we have to move a lot, and of course I was not used to it," Guimaraes said. Praising his midfield partners, he added: "They're both amazing players. I think Declan is a monster, he can run 15 kilometres in a game, and Martin Odegaard, he always can find space to penetrate the opposite side." Squad competition and European milestones With Martin Zubimendi and Bukayo Saka ruled out for the next few weeks with muscle injuries and David Raya sidelined by a shoulder issue, Guimaraes stressed that internal competition keeps standards high across the dressing room. Odegaard leads the Champions League with 17 defensive line-breaking passes this season, while Arsenal sit one goal shy of 400 in the competition, including qualifiers. Arsenal are unbeaten in 16 Champions League league-phase matches over more than two years and unbeaten in 19 European games overall excluding penalty shootouts. Avoiding defeat against Dortmund would make them just the third English side to reach 20 or more consecutive European Cup or Champions League matches without losing, following Manchester United (25) and Manchester City (26). item.title: Where Eagles pick in NFL draft 1st round. Can they get Jeremiah Smith?
item.description: PHILADELPHIA − You might think that the Eagles ruined their chance at a top-five pick in the 2027 NFL draft by beating the Pittsburgh Steelers. The Eagles dropped from the No. 5 pick in the NFL draft before that game to No. 9 afterwards, according to Tankathon.com. It's possible that the Eagles continue to drop into the early teens through the next two games, on Dec. 6 against the Arizona Cardinals and on Dec. 13 against the Indianapolis Colts . Both the Cardinals and the Colts are 3-8 heading into their games on Nov. 29, and both teams have less talent than the Eagles. Buy Philadelphia Eagles tickets And yet, the Eagles do have a way of getting into the top five of the draft even if they do end up picking in the low to mid teens in the first round. That, of course, has everything to do with the trades Eagles general manager Howie Roseman has made over the past several months. Roseman got a 2028 first-round pick and 2027 fifth rounder for A.J. Brown. He got a 2028 second-round pick and 2027 fifth rounder for Cam Jurgens. Most recently, Roseman got a 2027 first-rounder and 2029 second-rounder for Jordan Davis. That first-rounder comes from Jacksonville, which is currently at No. 24. In all, the Eagles have five first-round picks and five second-round picks combined in the drafts from 2027-29. That should be plenty of ammunition for the Eagles to move up. The Eagles' most obvious needs are on the offensive line and defensive line and at either cornerback or safety. But Roseman could also consider drafting quarterback Jalen Hurts' eventual successor considering it's a rare chance for the Eagles to draft that high. It's also possible that the Eagles could make a push to trade up for Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith, even though the Eagles have DeVonta Smith and used a first-round pick last spring (No. 20 overall) on Makai Lemon. After all, Roseman has constantly said that he doesn't draft for need as much as best player available. Here, then, is a look at 7 players the Eagles could either trade up for or stay at their current positions at No. 9 and 24: Jeremiah Smith, WR, Ohio State Many NFL draft analysts are calling Smith the best wide receiver since Julio Jones in 2011. Smith leads all of FBS with 1,482 yards receiving and 17 touchdowns. He's also 6-foot-4, 222 pounds, and thus the polar opposite of both DeVonta Smith and Makai Lemon. What it would take: This might be a bridge too far for the Eagles, especially if Tennessee gets the No. 1 pick. The Titans would love to give QB Cam Ward another weapon. But the Titans have plenty of needs, and possibly trading down to get multiple first-round picks, plus an extra second or third, could entice them. Drew Mestamaker, QB, Oklahoma State It's not just the question over Hurts' future as he recovers from blood clots that have spread to his lungs. It's also the money. item.title: ‘Not the image I’m trying to promote’ – Nons Miraj apologises over outfit
item.description: By Aniobi Angel Nigerian actress, Nons Miraj has apologised following backlash over her recent outfit at an event, describing the incident as an unexpected wardrobe malfunction caused by a fitting and styling mishap. The entertainer, in a statement via Instagram while addressing the controversy, said there was no intention to appear in a manner that contradicted the image and values she was working to establish. According to her, what was intended to be a beautiful outfit turned into an unfortunate situation due to issues with its fitting and styling. She explained that she decided to attend the event rather than disappoint the organisers and guests who had invited her, despite concerns about the outfit. “In trying to make the outfit work and embody the look, I didn’t fully anticipate how things would turn out,” she said. Reflecting on the incident, Nons Miraj admitted that she had learnt the importance of prioritising herself rather than feeling pressured to meet other people’s expectations. The content creator also maintained that she had been deliberate about redefining her public image, personal brand and fashion choices, stressing that the controversial appearance did not reflect the woman she was working towards becoming. “I understand that as someone in the public eye, my appearances carry a certain responsibility, and I don’t take that lightly. I also understand that people may have had expectations of me, and I respect their feelings,” she added. She appealed to her supporters and critics to allow her room to learn from the experience, describing herself as human and capable of making mistakes. Nons Miraj thanked those who had supported her and understood that the incident was an unfortunate situation rather than a deliberate attempt to promote a particular image. “This is not the image I am trying to promote, and it is certainly not the woman I am working towards becoming,” she said. The post ‘Not the image I’m trying to promote’ – Nons Miraj apologises over outfit appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Maryland women’s basketball vs. Monmouth preview
item.description: The University of Maryland Women’s Basketball Team defeated George Mason University 81-62 at The Xfinity Center on November 8th 2026. | Photo by Jessie Reider/Testudo Times No. 18 Maryland women’s basketball gears up for the last leg of its five-game homestand, this time for a game against Monmouth. The Terps are coming off a historic 70-point win over Morgan State Saturday, where they allowed zero points in a quarter for the first time in program history. They’ll look to keep that momentum rolling to start Thanksgiving week. Maryland tips off against Monmouth Tuesday at 7:00 p.m. on Big Ten Plus. Monmouth Hawks (5-1, 0-0 Coastal Athletic Association) 2025-26 record: 21-12 (12-6), fifth place in the CAA Head coach Cait Wetmore has led Monmouth to a great start to the 2026-27 season in her third year at the helm. She took over for now-Toledo head coach Ginny Boggess. Wetmore has kept the momentum alive after back-to-back winning seasons, including the Hawks’ second 20-win season in 15 years. So far in its 2026-27 campaign, Monmouth is undefeated against other mid-major and non-Division 1 teams. The Hawks beat Marist and Binghamton by over 20 points and Maryland Eastern Shore by 48. Their lone loss came by two points on the road against Rutgers. Unlike Maryland’s other mid-major opponents, Monmouth boasts a healthy mix of returning talent and veteran experience, with eight returning players and six upperclassmen. Players to watch Gigi Gamble, senior guard, 5-foot-5, no. 2 – The senior is in her second season with Monmouth and is currently ranked third in the country in points per game. Gamble averages 26.4 points per game on 54% shooting from the field and 47.1% shooting from beyond the arc. She scored 30 points while making 12 of 19 shots against Rutgers. Divine Dibula, senior forward, 6-foot-1, no. 13 – Dibula has spent four seasons with Monmouth and has grown into the Hawks’ primary post player. She carries a large offensive workload because of it. Dibula works almost entirely out of the post, scoring all but three of her baskets this season in the paint. She averages 14.8 points and seven rebounds per game. Vanessa McManus, junior guard, 5-foot-8, no. 0 – The Cal Poly transfer has gotten into a rhythm, scoring over 20 points in Monmouth’s last three games. She finished her last game against Maryland Eastern Shore with 21 points on six shot attempts, going a perfect 15-for-15 from the stripe. McManus averaged 15.9 points at Cal Poly last season and has averaged 14.8 points in Monmouth’s first six games. Strength Offensive efficiency. Monmouth averages over 87 points per game and ranks 19th in effective field goal percentage. All but three players who have seen the court for the Hawks are shooting over 50% from the field. item.title: Sean McVay says he’s ‘excited’ about Rams after season-ending injury to Puka Nacua
item.description: Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams are losing their star receiver for the season, but head coach Sean McVay is still excited for one key reason. The Los Angeles Rams are currently sitting at 6-4 in a tough division with the rampaging San Francisco 49ers and the reigning champion Seattle Seahawks. The team has had their share of injury issues pop up, most notably to star receiver Puka Nacua. In seven games this season, Nacua was averaging 10 receptions and just over 100 receiving yards per game. Nacua was initially diagnosed with multiple ligament sprains and turf toe after being injured on LA’s final offensive snap in Week 9 against the Commanders. Since then, it has been revealed that he will undergo MCL surgery and miss the rest of the season. Head coach Sean McVay is still ‘excited’. Sean McVay says he is ‘excited’ to see how the LA Rams respond to adversity and how other players step up Nacua being out isn’t the only concern plaguing McVay at the minute. Davante Adams has been out injured, and now even tight end Terrance Ferguson is set to undergo season-ending surgery. Their receiving options are looking extremely light at the minute, but McVay seems to have belief in his guys. Asked about the situation by The Athletic’s Nate Atkins, the head coach gave a surprising answer sharing his positive outlook regarding the remainder of the season. “Based on last week, I’m excited about what those guys that did get opportunities did,” McVay said. “Let’s continue to see if we can grow and figure out what it looks like. You know the information that I had at the time, but I don’t want it to ever be misunderstood. “I am confident in Tutu Atwell and Konata Mumpfield and Xavier Smith and C.J. Daniels, and (Brennan) Presley getting a chance to get back there and return kicks. It’s a bummer to lose those two significant pieces, but I think you have to adjust and adapt. “This is the hand that we’re dealt. I’m excited about trying to watch these guys go shine and do everything we can with our decision-making and our thought process to help bring that to life collectively for our group. A lot of that stuff, there have been some moving parts. “The Terrance Ferguson stuff I just found out 30 minutes ago. The Puka stuff was, you gather more information and you decide on getting that surgery. There has been a flexibility that’s been necessary. We’ll look forward to hopefully getting Davante (Adams) back at some point too.” The Rams have won four games in a row and have been rolling. McVay is known for being a great motivator, and it seems he is relishing the challenge of finding ways to win even while missing some key pieces. It is going to be a tough season for the Rams, but at least their HC isn’t throwing in the towel. item.title: Week 13 college fantasy football rankings: Devon Dampier, Dylan Riley lead rivalry week
item.description: Boise State running back Dylan Riley lands the top spot in the Week 13 college fantasy football rankings, and he gets a Colorado State defense that ranks last in FBS in adjusted EPA per play allowed, per Game on Paper . Oklahoma State’s Caleb Hawkins moves up to FLEX2 and Ohio State’s Jeremiah Smith climbs to FLEX3. Utah’s Devon Dampier jumps from QB22 to QB1, Duke’s Nate Sheppard slips from FLEX1 to FLEX4, and West Virginia’s Michael Hawkins Jr. falls from QB1 to QB33 in a tough matchup. MORE: College football rankings 2026: AP Top 25 poll entering Week 13 Week 13 FLEX rankings outlook Boise State Broncos running back Dylan Riley (0) warms up before a game against the Washington State Cougars | James Snook-Imagn Images Riley ran for 69 yards and set career highs with five catches and 89 receiving yards in Boise State’s 22-20 loss to San Diego State. The junior has 1,360 rushing yards this season. Colorado State gives up 7.81 yards per carry, the most of any FBS defense, so the Broncos’ lead back should have plenty of room in Fort Collins. Caleb Hawkins ran 22 times for 98 yards and two touchdowns and caught four passes for 33 yards as Oklahoma State rallied from a 17-point halftime deficit to beat Arizona State 30-27 in overtime . He played through an ankle injury in Tempe, and Kansas allows 5.04 yards per carry. Smith caught six passes for 165 yards and two touchdowns in a 31-28 loss at Nebraska, and his 17 touchdown catches tie Terry Glenn’s Ohio State single-season record . Michigan ranks 16th in adjusted EPA per play allowed, so the matchup keeps the junior receiver behind the top two backs. Sheppard ran 19 times for 116 yards in a 20-10 loss to Clemson. His 55-yard touchdown was his 20th rushing score of the season, a Duke single-season record. He slides to FLEX4 because Wake Forest holds opponents to 4.23 yards per carry and ranks fourth in ESPN’s FPI. Iowa State’s Aiden Flora ran for 171 yards and both Iowa State touchdowns in a 48-17 loss at UCF, and he leads the nation with 1,506 rushing yards. He left late in that game with a leg injury but walked off under his own power. The former walk-on checks in at FLEX5 against a Kansas State defense that allows 5.46 yards per carry. Oregon State’s Jesse Legree (FLEX6) caught five passes for 69 yards in a 31-24 win over Utah State, and he gets a Fresno State defense that allows 7.03 yards per dropback. North Texas’ Jahiem White falls from FLEX2 to FLEX7 against a UAB defense that allows 4.93 yards per carry. item.title: Rob Gronkowski says he knows why the Giants will beat the Cowboys and win the NFC East
item.description: Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images The NFC East provided some of the most impressive performances of the weekend, with all four of the teams from the division adding a win to their records. Most of the focus will remain on the New York Giants, who top the division, and the Dallas Cowboys. The Giants were able to pull off an impressive victory over the red-hot Jacksonville Jaguars, which was huge for their hopes of reaching the postseason. With a matter of weeks now remaining in the 2026 regular season, the NFC East is the Giants’ to lose. They have shown mixed form of late, but Rob Gronkowski has seen something that has convinced him John Harbaugh’s team will take the division. Rob Gronkowski expects the New York Giants to win NFC East The Cowboys may have impressed offensively against the Tennessee Titans on Sunday, but their performance has been taken with a huge pinch of salt by Gronkowski . Brian Schottenheimer’s team’s lack of consistency is proving a big concern for the former tight end. “I’m going to tell you this, Jules: the Giants are going to win the division. We’re not all in on the Cowboys. We’re not believers. We believe that the Cowboys are pretenders. I mean, yeah, they put up points. We already talked about it: it was against the Tennessee Titans. But they’re too up and down,” he said on The Gronk and Jules Show. “The Giants are a solid football team. You know, they play how they play. They win games by running the ball and utilising the targets they need to utilise in order to move the ball down the field. They’re a well-coached team, and that’s the difference. The Giants have better coaching than the Dallas Cowboys do, with their coaching staff.” Although the Giants are proving themselves to be a solid team, they have still left the door open for the Cowboys to potentially make a late push for the division. Recent losses against the New Orleans Saints and Washington Commanders were far from ideal. However, the Giants do still hold the lead in the division. With seven games remaining in the regular season, their destiny is in their own hands. However, they do still have the San Francisco 49ers, Seattle Seahawks, Detroit Lions and the Cowboys all still to play. item.title: Barcelona ready to file criminal complaint against Real Madrid president Florentino Perez over Negreira statements
item.description: Barcelona ready to file criminal complaint against Real Madrid president Florentino Perez over Negreira statements Barcelona are preparing to escalate their legal dispute with Real Madrid president Florentino Perez, with SPORT reporting that the club could file a criminal complaint against him for defamation if he refuses to withdraw his accusations against the Catalan side. As per the outlet, the two parties are scheduled to attend a conciliation hearing in Madrid on Wednesday, November 25. However, Perez is not expected to appear in person and will instead send a lawyer, who will maintain his position on the disputed comments. The hearing is set to be a significant moment in the growing institutional conflict between Barcelona and Real Madrid, with the possibility of criminal proceedings now moving closer. Barcelona await Perez’s response at the conciliation hearing The purpose of Wednesday’s meeting is to give Perez an opportunity to retract statements that Barcelona considers false and damaging to its reputation. If he refuses to do so, the club intends to proceed with a criminal complaint. The legal process began on June 12, when Barcelona, then managed by interim president Rafa Yuste, initiated proceedings following Perez’s public accusations . Barcelona and Florentino Perez are set for crucial legal confrontation over Negreira case. (Photo by FRANCK FIFE/AFP via Getty Images) The club subsequently received a November 25 hearing date from the court on September 23. For what it is worth, the conciliation meeting is a preliminary requirement before Barcelona can formally pursue a criminal complaint for alleged calumnia under Article 205 of Spain’s Penal Code. Perez is not legally required to attend personally and can be represented. Negreira case comments behind Barcelona’s legal action The dispute stems from Perez’s press conference on May 12 and an interview the following day, during which he made accusations concerning Barcelona’s alleged relationship with referees and the Negreira case. Barcelona considers those remarks defamatory and argues that they have damaged the club’s public image. Explaining its position when the legal action was initiated, the club stated, “The purpose of this lawsuit is for Mr. Perez to retract certain statements he made knowingly falsehood and that are slanderous and offensive to the Club’s image and reputation.” The club is also seeking specific answers from the Real Madrid president. Florentino Perez could face legal action from Barcelona over Negreira case comments. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Their legal demands ask Perez to acknowledge his statements and either correct them or identify the referees he referred to as the “Negreira Boys”. Barcelona further wants him to specify the matches and incidents in which he believes alleged corruption took place. Florentino Perez’s latest comments could deepen the conflict The dispute has not subsided in the months since Barcelona initiated legal proceedings.

item.title: Dovbyk’s agent looking for suitors in January
item.description: Dovbyk’s agent looking for suitors in January Artem Dovbyk also watched Bologna’s last match from the bench. The Ukrainian center-back is still waiting for his first start for the Felsinei; first Tedesco and then Palladino aren’t impressed by the former Girona player. Quite the opposite. The 1997-born player moved to the Rossoblu on loan this summer with an option to buy for €17 million, an option that will never be exercised and forces Roma to take direct interest to avoid further devaluing a €41 million investment. The Capitoline club, therefore, is looking for the best solution for Dovbyk, who is increasingly distant from Bologna. One of the issues to be resolved is his €3 million net salary, of which €2.5 million is paid by the Rossoblu. Interested clubs would have to pay half of that. Dovbyk appears destined to leave Bologna. As reported by Resto del Carlino , Venezia is looking for a striker and has made contact to explore possible options for signing the Ukrainian striker. The 1997-born player’s agent, however, is scouting clubs in Spain. Dovbyk, in fact, was pichichi (top scorer) in La Liga before moving to Italy and beginning his downward spiral. Valencia is considering a move, but there’s work to be done given the player’s substantial salary, to which Bologna is paying 2.5 for the entire season. The Spanish club, if they acquire Dovbyk, could release Duro. The first moves ahead of the winter transfer window are underway.

item.title: Bruins Veteran Quietly Emerging As Important Piece Of Marco Sturm's Lineup
item.description: Bruins Veteran Quietly Emerging As Important Piece Of Marco Sturm's Lineup originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Boston Bruins have received plenty of attention for their offensive production recently, but one of the more encouraging developments involves a veteran defenseman who spent portions of the season struggling to secure consistent playing time. Connor Clifton has appeared in four consecutive games, taking advantage of an opportunity to establish himself in head coach Marco Sturm's lineup. The 31-year-old returned to Boston during the offseason on a two-year contract, giving the Bruins another experienced right-handed defenseman. His recent performances suggest that he could become more than an occasional replacement when injuries or lineup changes create opportunities. Connor Clifton Making Most Of Increased Playing Time Clifton's recent stretch has provided some encouraging numbers. According to BostonBruins.com, he recorded 13 hits, six blocked shots, eight shots on goal and an assist over his past four appearances. "Maybe a little cliché, a lot of sacrifices along the way, but I do appreciate every moment I get to spend here." On Connor Clifton's growing consistency, match with Mason Lohrei –– and positive attitude that has carried the veteran through his career: https://t.co/mcy4QqVs8G — Belle Fraser (@bellefraser1) November 22, 2026 He also averaged slightly more than 16 minutes of ice time during that stretch, establishing a more consistent workload than he experienced earlier in the season. Clifton had not appeared in consecutive games since early October before his current run. The Bruins have significant competition for playing time on defense, which makes his recent progress particularly noteworthy. Sturm has also acknowledged Clifton's improvement, indicating that the veteran has performed increasingly well with each appearance. MORE : Bruins Receive Interesting Update On Future First-Round Draft Pick From Maple Leafs Mason Lohrei Partnership Could Benefit Bruins Perhaps the most interesting element of Clifton's recent success involves his partnership with Mason Lohrei. The two remained together on Boston's third defensive pairing during Sunday's practice. Lohrei provides offensive ability and a willingness to become involved in developing scoring opportunities. Clifton's more defensive-minded approach could complement those strengths, allowing Lohrei to play aggressively without leaving the Bruins unnecessarily exposed. Finding the right combination of complementary defensemen can be particularly valuable over a demanding regular season. Boston doesn't necessarily need every player on its blue line to provide the same attributes. Clifton understands his responsibilities and has the experience to recognize when his defensive partner needs additional support. The Bruins return to action Wednesday against the Winnipeg Jets, providing another opportunity for the partnership to develop

item.title: New Super Formula champion Kakunoshin Ohta’s goal: standing for Japan in IndyCar
item.description: Motorsport photo New Super Formula champion Kakunoshin Ohta says he wants to demonstrate the value of the Japanese racing scene as he continues to work towards his IndyCar dream. Honda-backed Ohta secured the title with a race to spare in Saturday’s opening contest of last weekend’s Suzuka finale with a second-place finish behind Ayumu Iwasa , and rounded off his title-winning campaign by finishing runner-up to Tomoki Nojiri on Sunday. Read Also: Super Formula Suzuka: Kakunoshin Ohta secures title in dramatic fashion as Ayumu Iwasa wins Race 1 Super Formula Suzuka: Tomoki Nojiri breaks drought with win in season finale With four wins and eight podiums across the 12-race campaign, Ohta concluded the year with a 29.5-point margin over outgoing champion Iwasa, also delivering Dandelion Racing its first drivers’ title since 2020 and its first ever clean sweep of drivers’ and teams’ prizes. Ohta has always been open about his goal of graduating to IndyCar, and has gained experience of American racing in the IMSA SportsCar Championship with five appearances for the works Meyer Shank Racing Acura team over the past two seasons. The 27-year-old from Kyoto reiterated that desire, pointing out that unlike the majority of Japanese drivers active abroad, he has spent almost his whole career racing at home. “I am not one of those drivers who went to Europe at an early stage of my career; I’ve grown up as a development driver within Japan,” said Ohta in his champion’s press conference. Kakunoshin Ohta, DOCOMO TEAM DANDELION RACING Kakunoshin Ohta, DOCOMO TEAM DANDELION RACING “Recently I’ve gained experience overseas, but the core of my development has been here in Japan, and I believe that by moving on to a bigger stage and achieving results there, I can demonstrate the true value of the Japanese racing environment. “Most of the Japanese drivers who excel overseas have spent most of their careers in Europe, or have experience in F1, but in my situation, I feel I have to show the real value of the Japanese racing scene to the world. “I respect European and American racing, but for a relatively small island country like Japan to draw so many spectators and sustain a professional racing scene, with manufacturers working to develop young talent, it makes me proud as a Japanese person. “I want to be able to contribute to the Japanese racing world by going on to be successful overseas as a driver brought up in Japan, so that’s my aim moving forward.” In the run-up to the final round of the season at Suzuka, there were suggestions that Ohta could land a full-time ride next year in either IndyCar or IMSA, despite the withdrawal of Acura at the end of the 2026 campaign. However, it now appears that Ohta will defend his championship in 2027, most likely as part of a double programme in Japan with Honda that also includes Super GT. item.title: Welshmen Donald & Salt demolish Australia as England level series
item.description: Aneurin Donald's fifty off 18 balls was the joint third-fastest for England in T20s [Getty Images] Second T20, Carrara Australia 184-8 (20 overs): Chaudhary 45 (35); Curran 2-29 England 188-2 (13.1 overs): Donald 85 (32); Meredith 1-18 England won by eight wickets; series level 1-1 Scorecard An astonishing opening partnership of 151 in 10 overs between England's Aneurin Donald and Phil Salt demolished Australia and levelled the T20 series on the Gold Coast. Welshman Donald blitzed 85 from 32 balls, including nine sixes, while his compatriot Salt made 58 off 30 as England cruised to their target of 184 in just 13.1 overs. Donald's 18-ball fifty was the joint third-fastest for England in the format as the pair raced to 79-0 in the powerplay, flogging Australia's wilting second-string bowling attack to all corners of the ground in a remarkable display of power hitting. Salt, who was dropped by Joel Davies on 10, was mostly able to watch from the non-striker's end before accelerating to a 24-ball half-century of his own, which came during a brutal over from spinner Davies that went for 31. Donald looked gutted to miss out on a century after he holed out to long-on off Riley Meredith's bowling, before Salt was brilliantly caught and bowled by Ben Dwarshuis an over later. England's phenomenal top order - which still awaits the return of Jos Buttler from injury - finished the job with ease as Tom Banton finished unbeaten on 26 off eight balls including a monstrous six for the winning runs. Australia's 184-8 looked competitive at the halfway mark on a surface that had assisted England's spinners and Sam Curran's slower balls - the hosts recovering from a stodgy middle over period after falling to 58-4 in the powerplay. Davies added a handy cameo of 38 before Dwarshuis whacked Curran's last three balls for six to finish strongly but within just a few overs of the chase, Donald and Salt had silenced a lively Australian crowd in style. The five-match series continues at the Gabba, Brisbane, on Friday. Destructive Donald makes his mark Donald made his T20 debut as a 29-year-old earlier this summer on the back of consistent county and Hundred performances, but struggled to really cement his place with 56 runs in four innings. Still, a player known for an incredible strike-rate in particular, he was backed by Harry Brook and Brendon McCullum to play freely and showcased that strength against an Australia attack that had no answers. Brook himself said he was "speechless" at the end of the game, high praise from one of the world's best, as Donald and Salt made what could have been a tricky chase look like a stroll in the park. Only three international T20s had been held at the Gold Coast's Carrara Oval previously so England were in relatively unknown territory. Not that it mattered to Donald who swatted Davies for four from his first ball to start the demolition, and carried on in his usual leg-side dominant fashion. item.title: Meet Aneurin Donald - the Welshman seizing England chance in Australia
item.description: Aneurin Donald has played for Glamorgan, Hampshire and - currently - Derbyshire [Getty] From Gorseinon cricket club in Swansea to some of the most famous grounds in Australia. That is the journey England's latest Welsh batter Aneurin Donald is preparing to complete when the T20 five-match series starts against Australia on Saturday. Donald made his England debut in the home three-match series against Sri Lanka but this tour represents a step up. It is 12,000 miles between the Swansea suburb and the Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG) where the first game is being played. It is a journey that has taken many years since starting at his local cricket club. He originally came down with his father Andrew to watch the local rugby club but became hooked on cricket. "Gorseinon means so much to me," said Donald, speaking to the BBC at the Welfare Ground, where the two clubs are based. "My family and friends are so involved down here and I spent so much time there growing up as a kid, playing rugby and cricket. "I try and get back there as much as I can. It's the lifeblood of the community and the reason I got the chances I did. "The basis that I gathered here, the time and energy I spent training in the winter got me on the rung to professional sport and now an international cap." England's Donald ready to savour Welsh homecoming The Gorseinon work ethic and Leigh Halfpenny effect The one-lane indoor net, now called the Alan Jones indoor cricket centre after Gorseinon’s other England batter, helped shape Donald’s talent. "That one little indoor net lane we had is probably the big reason as to why I've made it as far as I have," said Donald. "It was a little tin shed with probably a five-yard run-up where my brother [Gafyn] used to bowl into the middle of my bat. "It was a massive part of my career now." Those nets included training when others were relaxing. "If I had to put one thing down in my junior years and what separated me was probably coming down and training and being able to use that little indoor shed," he adds. "My dad installed a belief in me if I was training on a day nobody else is, you have added that little extra, whatever time of year. "We used to go down every week and I can remember training on Christmas Eve. "It was freezing cold and I remember being wrapped up in scarves and there was ice on our breath." While the Donalds were freezing inside, outside honing his kicking skills was a Wales rugby icon who also started his sporting journey at Gorseinon. "We used to see Leigh Halfpenny kicking for hours on end and it's probably a reminder that work ethic is what makes great players like him great," said Donald. "I can’t compare my career with his but I took inspiration from seeing him out there." The Donald family affair Aneurin Donald's family were on hand to watch him be presented with his first England cap before the opening T20 against Sri Lanka in September [Getty Images] Donald’s dedication has had to be matched by his resolve.
