item.title: Bayern Munich in talks with Jamal Musiala after turbulent week
item.description: Bayern Munich in talks with Jamal Musiala after turbulent week This has been a turbulent week for Bayern Munich. The Bavarian giants drew 1-1 against FC Koln at the Allianz Arena, but more than the results, they suffered tremendous blows. Michael Olise and Harry Kane both got injured, with the England striker set to be out of action for almost three-to-four months. However, it is the situation with Jamal Musiala that has caused huge attention among all football fans across the world. Jamal Musiala: The current scenario (Photo by Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images) While injuries to Olise and Kane have added to Bayern’s growing concerns, the uncertainty surrounding Musiala has opened an altogether different and far more delicate chapter for the club. The 23-year-old has endured a frustrating spell on the sidelines, with recurring absence seizures and the medical treatment required to manage his neurological condition raising questions about when he can return to his best. The issue has also spilled into the public domain, with several prominent figures at Bayern weighing in on how the club should approach the situation. Christian Falk has now shed further light on developments in an article for Bild , and he kindly shared the full picture with CFBayern Insider . The debate gathered pace 16 days ago when honorary president Uli Hoeneß, 74, questioned Musiala’s salary during an appearance on the BR programme Sonntags-Stammtisch . CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen, 59, later addressed the matter, but the discussion intensified on Friday when Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, 71, called for Bayern to hold talks with the player’s representatives about a possible adjustment to his contract or wages if his recurring seizures and ongoing treatment prevent him from consistently rediscovering his previous level. Those conversations have now moved beyond public statements and into the boardroom. BILD spotted Musiala’s agents, Christian Schmid and Tobias Altschäffl of 11WINS, arriving at Bayern’s administrative offices at Säbener Straße at 11:06am on Tuesday for a meeting that had been kept under wraps. The groundwork for the summit had already been laid internally. Bayern’s supervisory board discussed Musiala’s circumstances last Monday, following his second spell of absence within 12 weeks, although the club’s senior figures had not previously sat down with his representatives to discuss their concerns and expectations directly. Communication between the two camps has nevertheless remained regular since the illness first emerged, with the agency keeping Bayern informed about medical assessments and periods when the player has been unavailable. Until now, most of that dialogue has involved sporting directors Max Eberl and Christoph Freund, alongside head coach Vincent Kompany. Tuesday’s meeting, however, brought the club’s most senior decision-makers into the picture, with supervisory board chairman Herbert Hainer and Dreesen also expected to take part. item.title: Pakistan defeat sparks major shake-up: Tilak Varma makes three changes to India A XI vs UAE | Asia Cup Rising Stars
item.description: NEW DELHI: India A captain Tilak Varma made three changes to the playing XI for their crucial Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 Group B match against the United Arab Emirates in Doha on Tuesday. UAE captain Basil Hameed won the toss and elected to bat at the University of Doha for Science and Technology. India brought in Prabhsimran Singh, Harsh Dubey and Arshad Khan in place of Ayush Badoni, Vipraj Nigam and Prince Yadav. Asia Cup Rising Stars: Badoni, Nigam, Prince dropped after Pakistan defeat The changes came after India A suffered a 48-run defeat against Pakistan A in their previous match on Sunday. India had bowled Pakistan out for 313 in 49.2 overs but failed to chase down the target. Badoni and Vipraj both had disappointing outings with the bat, getting out for ducks. However, Vipraj did contribute with the ball, taking two wickets for 46 runs in his eight overs. Prince Yadav also picked up two wickets but conceded 60 runs in 9.2 overs. India will now look for a stronger all-round performance against the UAE. Asia Cup Rising Stars: India A's semifinal hopes at stake The defeat against Pakistan has put pressure on India's semifinal hopes, but they remain in contention for a place in the last four. India A have two points from two matches and need a win against the UAE to reach four points and secure qualification. Pakistan A have already booked their semifinal spot after winning both their group matches. The top two teams from Group B will advance to the semifinals, scheduled for November 26 and 27. Asia Cup Rising Stars: Where do India A stand in the points table? Pakistan A are at the top of Group B with four points from two matches. India A and Nepal have two points each, while the UAE are yet to open their account. Nepal kept their qualification hopes alive with a six-wicket win over the UAE on Sunday. Pakistan A then defeated India A to seal their place in the semifinals. India's positive net run rate of +2.580 gives them an advantage over Nepal and could prove important if the teams finish level on points. How can India A qualify for the semifinals? India A have several possible routes to the last four, with their match against the UAE playing a key role. 1. India A beat UAE and Pakistan A beat Nepal This is the simplest route. A win will take India A to four points and guarantee them a semifinal spot, regardless of the result of the other match. 2. India A beat UAE and Nepal beat Pakistan A In this situation, India A, Pakistan A and Nepal will all finish with four points. Net run rate will decide the final standings. India A will have an advantage because of their 306-run win over Nepal earlier in the tournament. Their current net run rate of +2.580 is much better than Nepal's -2.461. 3. India A's match against UAE is washed out and Pakistan A beat Nepal A washout will give India A one point, taking their tally to three. They will still qualify if Pakistan A beat Nepal, as Nepal will remain on two points. 4. UAE beat India A and Pakistan A

item.title: Tinubu seeks Reps’ approval for N65.17tn revised 2026 Budget
item.description: … retains N31.45tn deficit ….cuts 2026 budget by N3.15tn By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja President Bola Tinubu has transmitted a bill seeking to repeal and reenact the 2026 Appropriation Act to the House of Representatives, proposing a revised federal expenditure of N65.176tn. The President also forwarded a revised 2026 Federal Government Fiscal Framework to the House for consideration and approval. In a letter read on the floor of the House on Tuesday by the Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas, Tinubu said the proposed adjustments were aimed at aligning the 2026 budget with existing obligations and available resources. Under the revised fiscal framework, aggregate expenditure stands at N65.176tn, down from the N68.323tn approved in the original budget, while projected federal revenue, including receipts from government-owned enterprises, is put at N33.720tn. The revised budget also provides for aggregate capital expenditure of N26.232tn, while retaining the fiscal deficit of N31.457tn, representing 5.64 per cent of the Gross Domestic Product. Tinubu explained that the proposed adjustments would regularise some Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited expenditures incurred on behalf of the Federation, address underprovided debt-service obligations and recognise issued capital warrants and supplementation commitments. He said the revised framework would also provide for refunds to ministries, departments and agencies, as well as special accounts. According to the president, MDA capital provisions consist mainly of amounts already warranted, while a few new capital and overhead provisions were introduced as priority national interventions. He listed the interventions to include the completion of critical road projects, protection of agricultural production, reduction of production costs, improvement of farm yields, enhanced market access and measures to address water vulnerability. On borrowing, the President said the planned new borrowing remained unchanged at N29.218tn, comprising N18.428tn in domestic borrowing and N10.790tn in foreign borrowing. He further disclosed that the proposed $7.7bn external borrowing, equivalent to approximately N10.368tn at an exchange rate of N1,346.50 to the dollar, was intended to finance the existing foreign borrowing provision and would not increase the borrowing envelope. Tinubu said the adjustments were designed to prioritise existing commitments, improve the credibility and execution of the capital budget and maintain fiscal restraint. He consequently appealed to the lawmakers for expeditious consideration and passage of the bill to facilitate the orderly implementation of the revised budget and settlement of outstanding obligations. The post Tinubu seeks Reps’ approval for N65.17tn revised 2026 Budget appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Severe eczema healed by novel immune-calming pill in clinical trial
item.description: Eczema causes itchy, inflamed rashes on the skin Evgeniia Gordeeva/Getty Images Over a third of people with moderate to severe eczema taking part in a clinical trial have seen their skin completely or almost completely clear up after taking an experimental pill for four months. The drug targets a part of the immune system that causes eczema when it gets stuck in overdrive, and it may be preferable to the current standard treatment, which has to be injected. “It definitely looks promising,” says Gayle Ross at the Royal Melbourne Hospital. Read more Chronic inflammation messes with your mind. Here’s how to calm it Eczema, or atopic dermatitis, is a chronic skin condition characterised by itchy, inflamed rashes and broken skin that can become infected. It is driven by an overactive immune pathway involving two signalling proteins called interleukin-4 and interleukin-13. Advertisement In 2017, the companies Sanofi and Regeneron received approval in the US for their jointly developed eczema drug dupilumab, which blocks interleukin-4 and interleukin-13 signalling. But, although the medication is effective , it has had limited uptake in the US because it must be injected under the skin and costs up to $59,000 per year for those without insurance coverage. Now, another company, Kymera Therapeutics, has developed an alternative treatment that can be taken in pill form, called KT-621. It targets the same immune pathway as dupilumab but degrades a protein called STAT6 that is activated downstream from interleukin-4 and interleukin-13 in the development of eczema. Free newsletter Sign up to Health Check Sign up to newsletter In the clinical trial , 244 adults with an average age of 39 and moderate to severe eczema were randomised to take KT-621 at three different doses or a placebo pill every day for 16 weeks. Those taking the most effective dose experienced an average 72 per cent reduction in their eczema severity on a standard scale, compared to 27 per cent in the placebo group. What’s more, 38 per cent of participants taking KT-621 had completely healed skin or almost completely healed skin by the end of the trial. “These results exceeded our expectations,” said Terence Rooney , the chief medical officer of Kymera Therapeutics, when announcing the results in a webcast on 23 November. He showed before-and-after photos of one man who had had severe eczema all over his torso at the beginning of the trial, which disappeared by the end. “It’s obviously early days and the trial had relatively small patient numbers, but [KT-621] looks like it has similar efficacy to dupilumab, which is currently the standard of care for moderate to severe atopic dermatitis, and it would be nice to have an oral option as opposed to an injection,” says Ross. Read more You can upgrade your immune system, but not in the way you think The medication also appeared safe. item.title: Omo Agege: Delta Gov Condemns Political Killings, Orders Arrest Of Perpetrators
item.description: Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, has condemned political killings following Monday’s deadly political violence, which claimed several lives in the State. Oborevwori reacted when he visited Uuduere Community in Ughelli North Local Government Area on Tuesday. The governor first visited the area command office in Ughelli, where he held a closed-door meeting with the Commissioner of police, CP Samuel Etaifo Erale, and other senior security officers before proceeding to the community to assess the situation and interact with residents. Accompanied by the commander, 63 Brigade of the Nigerian Army, Brigadier General Ibrahim Buhari, the state director of the DSS and other security officials, Oborevwori described the incident as unacceptable and a grave threat to the peace and security of the state. He directed security agencies to intensify investigations, arrest all those involved, and ensure they are brought to justice. The governor lamented that political differences had degraded into violence and loss of lives, despite efforts to sustain peace in the state since 2023. he warned political actors against resorting to violence, stressing that no political ambition or disagreement could justify the destruction of lives and property. Oborevwori also reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to protecting lives and property, noting that peace and security remain essential to economic growth and development. Earlier, the delta state police command announced that it had commenced investigations into Monday’s attack on the campaign entourage of former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, during an NDC campaign rally in Uduere community. The incident reportedly left four persons dead and four others injured, while Omo-Agege was said to have escaped unhurt. the Omo-Agege campaign organisation described the incident as an assassination attempt, alleging that armed men opened fire on the campaign team. It also accused the Ughelli North Local Government Chairman, Jaro Egbo, of allegedly leading the attackers. The Chairman has denied the allegation. The NDC State chairman, Angirmaowei Richman Oyindoubra, had also called for the intervention of the Inspector-General of police, alleging that policemen deployed to the area were compromised. In response, the Delta State government has imposed a curfew in Ughelli North from 6:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. daily until further notice. The Commissioner of police, CP Samuel Etaifo Erale, has directed intensified security operations and warned political actors against thuggery, intimidation, and the unlawful use of firearms. Former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege has alleged that the gunmen who attacked his campaign team in Delta State, killing four people, repeatedly shouted his name and declared their intention to kill him. item.title: Nigeria can’t borrow its way out of economic crisis – Duke
item.description: The presidential candidate of Peoples Redemption Party, PRP, Donald Duke, has warned that Nigeria cannot borrow its way out of its economic crisis, urging the federal government to shift from debt-driven spending to policies capable of expanding production, creating wealth and strengthening the country’s revenue base. Duke, who was former governor of Cross River State, spoke in an interview in Abuja against the backdrop of the country’s rising debt burden and persistent economic pressures on households and businesses. He said: “Borrowing is not inherently wrong, but the critical question is what borrowed funds were being used for and whether they were generating sufficient economic returns. “Nigeria cannot continue contracting loans simply to sustain an economic structure that is failing to produce enough wealth and revenue. “Borrowing could be justified where funds were invested in productive infrastructure and other ventures capable of expanding the economy, but not using debt to finance inefficiency or recurrent expenditure.” Duke said the country must instead focus on increasing productivity, improving the business environment and expanding the number of Nigerians and businesses participating meaningfully in the formal economy. The PRP presidential candidate argued that Nigeria’s fiscal challenge was ultimately a production problem. “A country that does not produce enough cannot generate the revenue required to meet its obligations, regardless of how much money it borrows. “There is a need for a fundamental review of government expenditure. Public funds should be directed towards investments that increase productivity, create employment and generate additional revenue. “Government should broaden the revenue base without imposing measures that further weaken households and businesses. “The objective should be to create an economy in which businesses grow, employment expands and government revenues increase naturally as economic activity increases. “Continuing to rely heavily on borrowing without addressing these structural weaknesses would simply shift today’s problems to future generations,”he warned. The former Cross River governor said Nigeria needed to move away from an economic model centered on finding money to sustain government towards one focused on creating wealth. He said the country did not merely need more money in government coffers but a stronger productive economy capable of generating the resources required to finance development. “As a presidential candidate, I am concerned not merely with managing the current economic crisis but with changing the underlying structure that repeatedly produces it. “Nigerians deserve an economic system capable of creating sustainable opportunities rather than one that continually responds to hardship after it has occurred,” he said. The post Nigeria can’t borrow its way out of economic crisis – Duke appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: November’s full moon rises tonight! Here’s how to see the Beaver Moon supermoon
item.description: null Get ready stargazers! The full "Beaver supermoon" rises in the eastern sky, offering up a spectacular display shortly after sunset tonight (Nov. 24). Here's what you need to know. November's full moon occurs at 9:53 a.m. EST (1453 GMT) on Nov. 24, as the lunar disk passes opposite the sun in our sky, making it appear fully lit from our perspective. The November full moon is often referred to as the Beaver Moon because it rises around the time the small mammals are hard at work building their lodges in preparation for the winter. The Beaver Moon is also set to be a dazzling supermoon , because it turns full as the natural satellite passes within 90% of perigee , when it is at its closest to Earth in its 27-day elliptical orbit. A supermoon's proximity can make it appear 30% brighter and 14% larger than the most distant full moon of the year, which is colloquially known as a "micro-moon". When to see the Beaver Moon November's full moon will be below the horizon for stargazers in the U.S. at the moment it turns full. Instead, viewers in America should look out for the moon shortly after sunset on Nov. 24, as it looms low over the eastern horizon. A supermoon can make for a spectacular sight when caught close to the horizon. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech) Try covering the lunar disk with your thumb to block out the worst of its glare, and you may just be able to spot to blue-white lights of the Pleiades open star cluster glimmering less than 10 degrees away — roughly the width of your clenched fist held at arm's length. If you miss the full moon on Nov. 24, don't worry as the moon will appear full to the casual observer for a couple more nights, so there's no excuse to miss it! Remember to check out Time and Date's moonrise and moonset tracker for timings specific to your location. What should I expect from the November supermoon? You may see the moon turn a striking orange-yellow hue as it rises because sunlight reflected from its disk passes through more of Earth's atmosphere, which scatters shorter bluer wavelengths of light and allows more red and orange light to reach our eyes in a process called Rayleigh scattering. Celestron Nexstar 4SE (Image credit: Celestron) This is a fantastic go-to telescope with a 4-inch aperture and can help you quickly find a steady view of the moon. Check out our full Celestron Nexstar 4SE review for more. The supermoon will also appear particularly large while close to the horizon, as a phenomenon called the " moon illusion " tricks our brains into thinking that the lunar disk is larger while in the presence of foreground objects compared to when it is overhead. It'll make for a breathtaking photo opportunity, which you can capitalize on with our beginner's guide to imaging the full moon , along with our picks of the best cameras and lenses for capturing the night sky . item.description: Human rights activist and the presidential candidate of African Action Congress (AAC), Omoyele Sowore, has criticised Catholic Bishop of Sokoto Diocese, Bishop Matthew Hassan Kukah, over what he described as the silence of his peace committee amid escalating political violence and alleged assassination attempts in the country. Sowore called for the dissolution of the committee, questioning its relevance in the face of repeated attacks on political candidates and their supporters. In a short message sent to Vanguard, the activist said it was time to ask Kukah to shut down his peace committee, accusing it of failing to speak out against violence targeting political actors. He questioned the committee’s silence, asking where it was when candidates and their supporters came under attack. Sowore also declared that he would no longer participate in peace accord signing ceremonies, expressing dissatisfaction with what he considered the committee’s failure to respond to political violence. “For my part, I will never attend another peace accord signing event,” he said. He maintained that peace initiatives should demonstrate commitment to addressing violence and protecting political participants rather than merely organising public signing ceremonies. item.title: ‘I don’t care which party they belong to’ – Oborevwori vows arrest over Delta killings
item.description: Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, has vowed that everyone involved in the killing of six persons during a political gathering in Ughelli North Local Government Area will be arrested, regardless of their political affiliation or status. Oborevwori gave the assurance on Tuesday after meeting with security chiefs over Monday’s violence in Uduere community, where gunmen attacked a campaign gathering involving former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege. While speaking after the meeting, the governor insisted that nobody would be shielded from prosecution on account of their political connections. “We don’t care where they belong to. We don’t care the party. We don’t care about the level of the people who were arrested,” he said. The governor described the incident as unfortunate, saying more than six people had lost their lives. “It’s very sad that we lost over six persons. People know me, I’m not a violent person. And that’s the reason why in my agenda, the fourth pillar of my agenda is to enhance peace and security,” he said. The Nigeria Police Force had earlier confirmed that six people were killed and several others injured in the violence. The Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Ani Iniedu, said preliminary police reports indicated six deaths, adding that an investigation was underway to establish the verified casualty figure and determine the circumstances surrounding the incident. Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation had earlier reported that four members of the former deputy Senate president’s entourage were killed, naming two of them as Moses Anaughe and Akima Efemena Umukoro. It also identified four people as critically injured. The campaign organisation described the incident as an assassination attempt on Omo-Agege, who escaped unhurt. Oborevwori said the government had a constitutional responsibility to protect lives and property, citing Section 14(2)(b) of the 1999 Constitution, while also referencing citizens’ right to life under Section 33. He commended security agencies for their response and directed them to ensure that everyone found culpable was brought to justice. The governor also disclosed that a curfew had been imposed across Ughelli North Local Government Area, covering the affected community, to prevent further violence. “I assure Deltans, I assure the people of Ughelli that this will not happen again,” he said. He added that the killing of the community’s President-General was particularly painful and warned that political violence could undermine peace and discourage businesses and investors from operating in the state. Meanwhile, Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, has ordered a thorough and impartial investigation into the incident.y The police said the probe would identify those responsible, establish the sequence of events and examine the deployment and conduct of officers at the scene. item.title: 2027: Police will not be used as Political Tool – IGP
item.description: By Edwin Philip Abuja -The Inspector-General of Police (IGP) Olatunji Dusu has assured Nigerians that the Nigeria Police Force (NPF) will not serve as a political tool ahead of the 2027 general elections. Dusu was speaking on Tuesday at the day 2 of 2027 edition of Media Development Conference, organised by Centre for Journalism Innovation and Development (CJID) taking place at the Abuja Continental Hotel, Dusu emphasised that policing is anchored on public trust and accountability rather than force. ​Expressing commitments ahead of the 2027 elections, the IGP stated that the Nigeria Police Force will be guided by professionalism, neutrality, and accountability to all Nigerians, political parties, and the law. ​He said “Any police officer found to be partisan, to have taken sides, or to have aided any candidate or the party will face disciplinary action under the force’s code of conduct”. ​Addressing grievances surrounding the alleged misuse of the Cybercrime Law against journalists, Dusu pledged that the police under his leadership will not be a willing tool for oppression in the hands of politically motivated actors. He warned that elections can now be disrupted through the information environment—via fake videos, doctored audio, coordinated social media falsehoods, and fabricated stories capable of triggering real-world violence. Responding during the panel session which was on ‘People centred public safety and State policing in Nigeria’, the Nigerian Police boss, said that Nigerians should not be afraid of the State Governors misusing the State policing system, he assured that safeguards are being developed to ensure state police structures are not hijacked for personal or political interests, including provisions for federal intervention if situations get out of hand. IGP noted that the National Assembly, and the nation are working to design a framework suited specifically to Nigeria’s realities rather than copying foreign models, emphasising that police training will be standardised across the country so that officers in states such as Lagos and Kano undergo uniform training standards regardless of differing local functions. On the enforcement of the Cybercrime Act, the IGP disclosed that the force has held two symposiums since his assumption of office to examine cybercrime laws and digital offenses. He urged citizens and media practitioners to familiarize themselves with the provisions of the Act, noting that actions often perceived as minor online can constitute offenses under the law. He added that personnel posted to the NPF cyber section are being trained and equipped to tackle emerging digital crimes. IGP Dusu affirmed that journalism is not a crime and described journalists as essential partners in progress and development who hold governments accountable. While acknowledging that press freedom in Nigeria is relatively better than in some neighbouring countries in the Sahel region, he noted there is still room for improvement on both

item.title: Police arrest 11 suspected yahoo boys in Ogun, recover charms
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Police Special Fraud Unit (PSFU), under FCID Alagbon, has arrested 11 suspected internet fraudsters during an intelligence-led raid on an alleged cybercrime hideout, popularly known as a “Yahoo academy,” in Abeokuta, Ogun State. The operation also led to the recovery of suspected fetish materials, including charms, blood-stained items and suspected human remains, alongside 11 iPhones, three Samsung mobile phones, eight laptops and a 2014 Lexus RX 350. The suspects were reportedly arrested at House 10, Second Hill Estate, Oloke-Meji, Onikolobo, Abeokuta, following investigations by detectives of the police unit. According to the police, the suspects were allegedly members of an organised internet fraud network known as “Hustle Kingdom”, which operated from the apartment and used the facility as a base for cyber-enabled fraud and other criminal activities. The Police Public Relations Officer of the PSFU, DSP Ovie Ewhubare, disclosed this in a statement made available to newsmen, saying preliminary investigations indicated that the suspects exploited the identities and personal information of foreign nationals to defraud unsuspecting victims online. The statement identified the arrested suspects as Adedolapo Samuel, 25; Timothy Babatunde, 27; Ibrahim Sholete, 30; Torioza Oluwatosin, 30; Yusuf Alabi, 30; Adeyemi Seyi, 32; Tobiloba Oguntoyinbo, 32; Taiwo Mathew, 23; Shoyombo Ayomide, 24; Abayomi Rahmon, 32; and Abolaji Tunji, 28. It, however, disclosed that the alleged leader of the group, identified as Goriola Oluwaseun Olanrewaju, popularly known as “Update”, was still at large. The police said Olanrewaju allegedly rented the property in 2021 before recruiting young men into the criminal network. The statement read in part: “Investigations revealed that one Goriola Oluwaseun Olanrewaju ‘M’, also known as Update, currently at large, rented the apartment in 2021 and subsequently recruited young men into an organised internet fraud operation, commonly known as a ‘Hustle Kingdom’, where they use the facility as a base for cyber-related fraud and other criminal activities. “The suspects admitted that they exploit the identities and personal details of foreign nationals to defraud unsuspecting victims online.” Reacting to the development, the Commissioner of Police, Eloho Okpoziakpo, said the operation underscored the importance of credible information, intelligence-led policing and professional investigative skills in tackling organised financial crimes and other cyber-enabled offences. Okpoziakpo said investigations were ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the occupation of the property and determine whether its owners had discharged their responsibilities by verifying the identities of their tenants and monitoring activities on the premises. item.title: Champions League: Arsenal face tough Dortmund test as Man City welcome Napoli
item.description: Arsenal will face a stern test when they host Borussia Dortmund in the UEFA Champions League on Tuesday, while Manchester City welcome Italian champions Napoli to the Etihad Stadium as the competition enters Matchday Five. The two fixtures headline Tuesday’s European action, with both Premier League sides seeking important victories to strengthen their positions in the league phase. Arsenal, who currently occupy third position with 10 points from four matches, will be looking to maintain their impressive European run when they welcome Dortmund to the Emirates Stadium. Mikel Arteta’s side have recorded three victories and a draw in their opening four Champions League matches, beating Napoli, Lille and Slavia Prague before playing out a 2-2 draw against Bayern Munich. The Gunners, however, will be without goalkeeper David Raya, who sustained a shoulder injury during their recent encounter with Newcastle United. Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are also listed among their unavailable players ahead of the Dortmund clash. Dortmund, meanwhile, arrive in London in good form after moving to the top of the Bundesliga with a 1-0 victory over Borussia Monchengladbach at the weekend. The German side have also won three of their four Champions League matches, beating Real Betis, Sabah and Villarreal, although they suffered a 1-0 defeat to Bodo/Glimt. They currently sit one point behind Arsenal and will be hoping to close the gap with a positive result in London. The encounter will also offer an interesting reunion for Arsenal youngster Ethan Nwaneri, who is spending the season on loan at Dortmund and is eligible to feature against his parent club. Meanwhile, Manchester City will welcome Napoli in another important encounter at the Etihad Stadium. Enzo Maresca’s side occupy seventh position with nine points, while Napoli are 27th with three points after winning just one of their opening four matches. City head into the fixture after a 1-1 draw against Fulham in the Premier League, having struggled for consistency in recent domestic outings. They will, however, take confidence from their 3-2 victory over RB Leipzig in their previous Champions League fixture as they look to strengthen their chances of securing automatic qualification for the round of 16. City will be without Antoine Semenyo, who is sidelined with a knee injury, while Matheus Nunes remains a doubt. For Napoli, the trip to Manchester presents an opportunity to revive their European campaign after defeats to Arsenal, Villarreal and Porto. The Italian side secured a 1-0 victory over Torino in Serie A at the weekend but face a difficult assignment against Guardiola’s men. Former Manchester City midfielder Kevin De Bruyne is expected to feature for Napoli, adding another interesting storyline to the encounter. However, Napoli will be without several players, including Giovanni Di Lorenzo, Stanislav Lobotka and Alex Meret, while defender Rafa Marin is suspended. Both matches are scheduled to kick off a

item.title: Bayern score ‘own goal’ as Musiala firestorm builds
item.description: Already ravaged by injuries, Bayern Munich head to Lille in the Champions League on Wednesday swept up in a firestorm of their own making over star midfielder Jamal Musiala. Currently 13th in the table, Bayern need points if they are to reach the top eight and avoid a punishing extra knockout round. While Lille are languishing in 35th spot, last season’s semi-finalists Bayern limp into the clash despite being one of the leading contenders. Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane was the latest to join Bayern’s bulging casualty ward with an ankle injury on Friday which will likely rule him out until February. But while Musiala returned after a two-month absence in last week’s match, club bosses were accused of launching a coordinated effort to pressure the midfielder into accepting a pay cut. That the club decided to kick-start the furore a day before announcing record revenues of close to a billion euros has not gone unnoticed. – ‘Own goal’ – In August, Musiala revealed he was suffering from a “neurological disorder” which can lead to “temporary but treatable seizures”, having collapsed twice on the field in pre-season. After his return, club powerbroker Karl-Heinz Rummenigge told German TV the 23-year-old midfielder was unlikely to recapture his previous form due to the condition — and should consider taking a pay cut. “If he doesn’t return to being the Jamal of old, then we need to have a conversation with his family, with the player, and, above all, with his agency — because, frankly, the current financial figures would no longer be justifiable,” Rummenigge told Sky Germany. Rummenigge’s statements were striking but echoed those made by former president and fellow powerbroker Uli Hoeness, along with current CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen. On Sunday, player union FIFPRO slammed Bayern, accusing the club of a “coordinated campaign to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives” to accept a wage cut. “A club of Bayern’s standing should know better,” FIFPRO said in a statement. FIFPRO’s German counterparts VDV joined the chorus on Monday, saying the comments would “leave a lasting impression” on Musiala and on the club in general. “I believe those in charge have scored a real ‘own goal’ here,” VDV president Carsten Ramelow said in a statement. World Cup and Ballon d’Or winner Lothar Matthaeus, who has never been afraid to butt heads with Hoeness and the Bayern brass, said the club should provide Musiala with “every bit of support.” “Right now, everything is being placed on Musiala’s shoulders,” Matthaeus told RTL. “Perhaps all parties can sit down and talk later at a more opportune moment,” he added. – An opportunity for Musiala – For their part, Bayern coach Vincent Kompany and powerful sporting director Max Eberl have thrown their support behind Musiala publicly. item.title: Questions Linger After Jensen Huang’s Return To Nvidia
item.description: Jensen Huang’s surprise return to Nvidia on Monday appeared to stabilize the US chip giant, along with the broader stock market and AI ecosystem, but questions linger about the longterm impact of his scandal. Is Nvidia in the clear? An internal investigation overseen by independent directors is still underway at Nvidia regarding concerns that Huang might have been the target of an espionage campaign by China. US government officials, including President Donald Trump, assured Nvidia’s board that reinstating the company’s cofounder “poses no national security risk.” Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang (R) speaks alongside US President Donald Trump about investing in America, at the White House in Washington, DC, on April 30, 2025. Photo by JIM WATSON / AFP In parallel, the US Department of Justice is investigating Megaspeed, a company based in Singapore that allegedly bought processors from Nvidia and routed them to Chinese customers, circumventing US export restrictions. The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has also reportedly launched an investigation into Nvidia’s accounting practices and potentially misleading communication to shareholders. However, the Trump administration has generally avoided going after its allies, so the federal probes might not result in much, Columbia University Professor Eric Talley said. Will Huang be held accountable? Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang speaks during Nvidia Live at CES 2026 ahead of the annual Consumer Electronics Show in Las Vegas, Nevada, on January 5, 2026. The embattled chief will nevertheless have to explain himself to lawmakers at a closed-door hearing on December 1 before three House committees. He will also testify before a Senate committee on December 3 in a hearing that will be livestreamed, while California’s attorney general has opened an investigation into the company’s chip exports and shareholder disclosures. There are plenty of regulators who are willing to push back against the Trump administration and ask tough questions, Talley said. Trump is also known to flip on people whom he no longer considers friends. “He can become estranged with people, and if that would happen with Jensen Huang, I can imagine a boomerang” on the Trump administration’s approach, Talley said. What does the board’s future look like? The logo of Nvidia is seen during a production preview exhibition in Taipei on May 21, 2025. Photo by I-HWA CHENG / AFP Openly opposed to Huang’s return before ultimately reinstating him, the board is in a delicate position. Former Goldman Sachs chief Lloyd Blankfein predicts its days may be numbered. A revolt by shareholders, many of whom supported the reinstatement of the 63-year-old entrepreneur, could reshape the board as soon as 2027, since all directors stand for reappointment every year. If they are spared, the directors could keep Huang on a much “shorter leash” compared to its history of largely deferring to the overwhelming power of this extraordinary executive, Talley said.

item.title: UK gov invests in defense startup making virtual training ground for AI
item.description: The British government is investing in a UK-based AI defense startup that aims to train autonomous military systems in virtual environments, in a bid to reduce the country's reliance on overseas technology. Both the Sovereign AI Fund and the National Security Strategic Investment Fund (NSSIF) have contributed to a Series A funding round for Agon Dynamics, said to value the biz at $450 million. This $70 million round takes the total capital raised by the firm to $100 million, following its initial $30 million seed round earlier this year. The government claims this move will help strengthen the UK’s sovereign capabilities when it comes to the use of AI for defense, plus the hope that nurturing native technical know-how converts into industrial strength and greater resilience. But it is not revealing how much cash it has stumped up, claiming such investments are commercially sensitive, although it did say that typical equity amounts obtained from the the Sovereign AI Fund tend to be worth around £1 million to £10 million ($1.3 million to $13 million). Agon is understood to be developing facilities to train and test AI systems needed for defense. This covers systems to help defend against drone attacks, or ensuring that AI tools still continue to work as intended if communications with the command center are disrupted. Training like this currently needs to be carried out in the real world, which is time-consuming and expensive, according to the government. For this reason, Agon is building a "virtual battlefield" environment where AI models can be tested against realistic simulations of the situations they might encounter. The company says its synthetic battle arena provides a safe, repeatable environment for developers and defense contractors to try out autonomous systems against thousands of demanding scenarios before deployment. Systems can face adaptive virtual adversaries informed by live conflict intelligence, helping them to respond to evolving tactics, threats and operating conditions. This may include simulations of mass drone attacks that would overwhelm conventional air defense systems, or testing how autonomous systems operate when navigation is degraded or adversary tactics change. "Europe is in an AI arms race as we enter the era of agentic warfare: intelligent agents and machines that will need to understand their environment, make decisions and adapt at a speed and scale that humans alone cannot match," says co-founder and CEO Tristam Constant, a former British Army officer. "We exist to build the sovereign infrastructure and AI foundation models to allow us to train, test, and evolve autonomous defense systems, in Europe, for Europe - to outperform adversary capabilities." For the government, AI Minister Kanishka Narayan claimed that Britain is well-placed to lead efforts to ensure such technologies are reliable, trustworthy, and deployed responsibly. item.title: Canada PM brings Trump impersonator on stage during press gala
item.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney invited a Donald Trump impersonator on stage during a weekend press gala, a move one critic said risks provoking a president known to bristle at being mocked. Carney was making a lighthearted speech at the Canadian equivalent of the White House Correspondents’ Dinner when he announced he was pressing an “emergency comedy button.” Comedian Mark McKinney, who impersonates Carney, came out first, followed by Trump impersonator Mark Critch, who appears on the long-running Canadian sketch comedy show “This Hour Has 22 Minutes.” “We’ve got two Carneys here, it’s a disaster,” Critch joked as Trump, before taking shots at Washington’s controversial ambassador to Canada and the White House press secretary vacancy, after Katie Zacharia left the role in just five days. With the United States and Canada still locked in a trade war, Critch offered some comic assurances about an impending pact. “Mark, we’re gonna have an incredible deal,” he said, mimicking Trump. “There’s only one thing standing in the way — me, because I’m crazy.” The bit appeared to go down well with reporters in Ottawa, but one of Carney’s political rivals was unimpressed. “I think provoking President Trump is arrogant, stupid and not funny,” said Yves-Francois Blanchet, the leader of the separatist Bloc Quebecois. He noted that Trump’s tariffs, including those affecting an aluminum industry central to Quebec’s economy, are causing real economic pain. “Quebec is paying the highest price for these tariffs…which should not be inflamed with bad jokes,” Blanchet said. Trump and Carney have both offered optimism that trade talks are progressing, but there were similarly positive comments in the days before negotiations collapsed in August. Canada wants relief from tariffs on key sectors, notably autos, but Ottawa has warned that completely removing the levies is unlikely and the Canadian economy needs to adjust to a permanently altered trading relationship with the United States. The post Canada PM brings Trump impersonator on stage during press gala appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Six killed, several injured in Delta political campaign clash – Police
item.description: The Nigeria Police Force has confirmed that six people died and several others sustained injuries during a violent incident at a political campaign event in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State. The Force also said the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, had ordered a comprehensive investigation into the incident, including the actions of police officers deployed to the venue. CSP Ani Iniedu, the Force Public Relations Officer, disclosed this in a statement on Tuesday, adding that preliminary police findings indicated that six people were killed. “Preliminary Police reports indicate that six persons lost their lives, while several others sustained injuries. “The Force is aware of varying casualty figures circulating in the public domain. An ongoing investigation will establish the verified number of casualties and determine the circumstances surrounding the incident,” the statement read. Iniedu said the IGP had instructed the Delta State Commissioner of Police to conduct a thorough, impartial and evidence-based investigation. He added that the probe would examine the sequence of events, establish the identities of those involved and determine the circumstances surrounding the shooting, including the actions and deployment of police personnel at the scene. The Force also confirmed that the Delta State Government had imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew across Ughelli North Local Government Area, running from 6pm to 6am daily until further notice. “In response to the security situation, the Delta State Government has imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew across Ughelli North Local Government Area, from 6:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. daily, until further notice. The Delta State Police Command is enforcing the directive and has intensified security measures to prevent further breakdown of law and order,” the statement read. The police urged residents, community leaders, political stakeholders and campaign groups to remain peaceful, obey the curfew and refrain from circulating unverified reports that could worsen tensions. It also called on anyone with useful information, photographs, video footage or other evidence to assist the investigation by submitting them through established police channels, assuring that the identity of informants would be protected. The police confirmation followed an earlier allegation by the campaign organisation of former Deputy President of the Senate, Ovie Omo-Agege, that gunmen attacked his entourage during a campaign tour of the area. The organisation had put the death toll at four, including two of its aides, identified as Moses Anaughe and Akima Efemena Umukoro, while claiming that four other people sustained critical injuries. item.title: ‎After Daily Trust story, foundation sponsors surgery for Kano teen battling facial tumour
item.description: ‎The Ihsan Scholarship Foundation, Kano, has sponsored the life-changing surgery of Salisu Sani, an 18-year-old whose struggle with a debilitating facial tumour was highlighted by Daily Trust, restoring hope to the teenager and offering him a chance to rebuild his future. ‎‎Daily Trust had reported how Salisu Sani, an indigene of Yalwa town in Tofa Local Government Area of Kano State, spent his days along Gandun Albasa Street in Kano soliciting support for a critical surgery after a massive tumour on his face left him in constant pain and threatened his eyesight. ‎‎Following the publication, a Kano-based foundation known for its humanitarian and educational interventions reached out to the teenager and took over the responsibility of his treatment. ‎The foundation, which requested anonymity, facilitated his return to the [Aminu Kano Teaching Hospital (AKTH), where medical evaluations were conducted and the much-needed surgery was successfully carried out. ‎Medical records obtained by Daily Trust showed that specialists at the hospital diagnosed the condition as Aggressive Trabecular Ossifying Fibroma, a rare fibro-osseous tumour affecting the jaw and facial bones. ‎The pathology report indicated that tissue samples removed during surgery weighed about 640 grams. ‎‎Family members expressed gratitude to the foundation, medical personnel and members of the public who showed concern after the story was published. ‎Speaking after the successful operation, Salisu Sani said the intervention had given him a new lease of life. ‎“I never imagined that help would come this fast. For years I lived with the pain and the burden of carrying this tumour on my face. Today, I feel hopeful again,” he said. ‎The teenager had earlier told Daily Trust that the illness had forced him out of school and shattered his dreams, as his family could not afford the cost of treatment. ‎In a further boost to his recovery and future, the foundation also pledged to support his long-term rehabilitation by either sponsoring his education or providing him with full startup capital to establish a business and become self-reliant. ‎‎A representative of the foundation said the decision was informed by the need to ensure that the teenager not only receives medical care but also has the opportunity to build a productive life after recovery. ‎‎“Our concern is not limited to the surgery alone. We want him to be able to stand on his own feet and pursue his dreams. Whether through formal education or entrepreneurship, we will support him to become self-reliant,” the representative said.

item.title: Education software supplier's legacy login system left 355,000 school email addresses exposed
item.description: More than 355,000 school staff and pupil email addresses ended up in the hands of hackers who broke into UK education software supplier Bromcom in September. The breach was added to Have I Been Pwned on Monday, revealing that 355,051 unique email addresses were caught up in the incident. The data also included single sign-on (SSO) registration reference numbers, although Bromcom insists that no passwords or authentication tokens were stolen. As The Register reported in Octobe r , the attackers got in through a legacy SSO registration component in Bromcom's Communications Server environment. The technology had already been superseded but was still running because an internal system continued to use it. Bromcom discovered something was amiss on September 6 after customers reported problems accessing its SSO service. At the time, the company was still working with external forensic specialists to establish exactly what the intruders had managed to get their hands on. Bromcom's FAQ says its investigation is complete and confirms that the intruders used a script to extract SSO registration information from the compromised server. The supplier insists its Management Information System (MIS), used by schools to keep track of everything from attendance to pupil records, was untouched. The compromised service also couldn't be used to get into Microsoft or Google accounts, which have their own login systems. Bromcom has since pulled the plug on the old component, tightened its authorization checks, and added more security logging. It says it hasn't found any evidence of accounts being hijacked as a result of the breach. Bromcom also confirmed it hadn't reported the breach to the UK's Information Commission's Office. Its reasoning is that it was the data processor, not the controller, so any decision to involve the regulator was for the affected schools and academy trusts to make. As for the risk to staff and pupils, Bromcom considers it to be low. No passwords or pupil records held in the MIS were taken, it says, although schools have been advised to watch for phishing messages and suspicious requests to reset passwords or approve sign-ins. The supplier's software is used by more than 5,000 schools and 390 multi-academy trusts across the UK, though it hasn't said how many were caught up in this particular mess. The Register has asked Bromcom how many schools and pupils were affected, and whether the figure published by Have I Been Pwned matches its own findings, but has yet to receive a response. Bromcom kept the superseded component running because an internal system still needed it. Unfortunately, the intruders found a use for it too. ®

item.title: ‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍⁠⁠​​‌⁠‌INEC to conduct mock accreditation in 490 Lagos polling units
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) says it will conduct a mock accreditation and result upload exercise in 490 polling units across Lagos State on Saturday. Prof. Ayobami Salami, the Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) in Lagos State, disclosed this in an interview with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Tuesday in Lagos. Salami said the exercise would take place between 8:30 a.m. and 2:30 p.m. in selected polling units across the state. He said it was designed to assess the performance of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and identify possible gaps or challenges that would be addressed before the 2027 general elections. According to him, the exercise will cover the 245 Registration Areas (RAs) across the state’s 20 Local Government Areas (LGAs), with two polling units selected in each Registration Area. He urged residents, particularly eligible voters in the selected polling units, to participate in the exercise to enable the commission to assess the effectiveness of its equipment and electoral processes. The REC said the list of selected polling units would be displayed at the respective local government area offices to enable residents to identify the designated locations. Salami said he had directed all electoral officers in the state to convene stakeholder meetings in their respective LGAs ahead of the exercise. He said the meetings would provide an opportunity to engage political parties and other stakeholders on the importance of participating in the mock accreditation exercise. The REC said the engagements would also help mobilise eligible voters in the selected polling units to participate in the exercise. He outlined the activities preceding the exercise, saying BVAS configuration would take place on Nov. 25, followed by the training of nominated personnel on Nov. 26. According to him, personnel and devices would be deployed to the selected polling units on Friday, ahead of the exercise. Salami reiterated that the exercise formed part of INEC’s preparations to ensure a smooth and efficient electoral process during the 2027 general elections. item.title: The Design Table 2026 by So.Me Solutions: African Fashion in the Spotlight with $7,000 in Award Support for Emerging Designers
item.description: The Design Table 2026 brought together some of the voices, ideas and creative forces shaping African fashion for an afternoon of industry exchange, recognition and conversation. The annual cultural platform, produced by So.Me Solutions, welcomed designers, fashion entrepreneurs, industry leaders, media personalities and fashion enthusiasts for its latest edition. Held at GRAS Lagos, Victoria Island, during Lagos Fashion Week, this year’s gathering explored the people, perspectives and opportunities influencing the future of African fashion. The event also marked a significant milestone for So.Me Solutions, which celebrates 10 years as a 360 communications agency. Among the guests were Folake Amber (Tiffany Amber), Bola Balogun (Glam Brand), Sharon Adeleke, Beverly Naya, Awed by Moni, Marvy Olugu (House of Marvee) and Funmi Ford , alongside other familiar faces from across fashion, entertainment and the creative scene. A Seat at the Table for the Next Generation A major highlight of this year’s edition was the Next Gen Design Impact Award, which received 101 applications from emerging designers. Following the selection process, three finalists, Sultana, Dimeji Ilori and Bjuv Woman , were shortlisted for the award. The finalists were evaluated by a five-member jury comprising Dr. Yetty Ogunnubi, Odio Mimonet, Eniafe Momodu, Ugonna-Ora Owoh and Yoanna “Pepper”, with guests also participating in the voting process. Bhuv Woman emerged as the winner, receiving the $5,000 grand prize funded by Vlisco, Patrón and Culture Lab. In addition, Odio Mimonet extended a further $2,000 in award support, bringing the total prize support associated with the award to $7,000. Beyond the financial support, the winning package includes mentorship, industry access and opportunities to further advance the designer’s work. The announcement was an emotional moment for Bhuv Woman, who was visibly moved as she received the recognition and expressed gratitude to the organisers. Through the award, The Design Table continues to create opportunities for emerging designers to gain visibility, access and recognition while connecting them with established voices and resources within the fashion industry. Who Gets to Shape the Future of African Fashion? The conversations continued with a speakers session titled “ Who Gets to Shape the Future of African Fashion?” , moderated by Yvan Otu and featured Mai Atafo , founder of ATAFO; Ezinne Chinkata , founder of Zinkata; Sacha Okoh, fashion entrepreneur and creative director of Viva; Kiki Osinbajo , founder of CIAR; and Tess Tanaka, founder of Moda54. The session explored how African fashion can move beyond being treated as a niche category and become more firmly integrated into the wider global fashion landscape. Discussions touched on what it takes for African brands to be stocked, worn and embraced as part of everyday fashion, alongside the realities of production, pricing, distribution, customer experience and access to markets. item.title: YouTube star Ms Rachel protests US child immigration hearings
item.description: Ms Rachel, the American creator of hit sing-songy educational videos for toddlers, attacked the use of immigration hearings for children following a courthouse visit on Monday. “I’ve seen children who are just missing the light in their eyes and they’re begging to go to the spelling bee or to just, you know, be with their younger siblings,” said Ms Rachel, who is known offline as Rachel Accurso. “They’re just so scared and praying to God, that they, please change the hearts of ICE (Immigration and Customs Enforcement) and let us out,” added the 43-year-old after observing legal procedures of juveniles being processed through the immigration courts. Her appearance at the New York youth immigration court was part of an effort to shine light on the Trump administration’s immigration policy that was supported by newly elected US lawmaker Brad Lander. Lander criticized a “travesty of justice” as cases are sped up while funding for legal representation is cut. In videos uploaded to her 22 million subscribers on YouTube, Ms Rachel, known for her signature pink headband and denim overalls, teaches infants to identify animals, colors, and numbers. On her other social media platforms, she is taking an increasingly vocal stand for children’s rights. She has notably led a fundraiser for the organization Save the Children in support of Palestinian children in Gaza and has backed campaigns critical of US migrant detention centers where children are kept, decrying poor conditions and calling for their closure. Targeted by a smear campaign for her pro-Gaza stance, Ms Rachel said previously that it would be more controversial to say nothing. “I think it’s sad to take someone’s dedication and love for all children and try and make that wrong,” she told PBS last year. The post YouTube star Ms Rachel protests US child immigration hearings appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Paris Club Refunds: Court freezes N135.5bn linked to Governors’ Forum
item.description: …restrains 29 banks By Taiye Agbaje An Abuja High Court has ordered an interim freeze on N135.5 billion paid to the Nigerian Governors’ Forum (NGF) as a stakeholder in the Paris Club refunds dispute. Justice O. C. Agbaza granted the interim Mareva injunction following an ex-parte application brought by Dr Ted Iseghohi-Edwards. The order restrained the Incorporated Trustees of the NGF from withdrawing, transferring, dissipating or otherwise dealing with the funds. The order also restrained 29 commercial banks from releasing, transferring, converting or otherwise dealing with funds belonging to the NGF within their custody. The judge further directed the banks to disclose, within 48 hours of service, whether the NGF maintains accounts containing the disputed funds. The banks are required to identify such accounts, their currencies, available balances and amounts preserved under the court’s order. The amount represents 100 million dollars, equivalent to the N135.55 billion, calculated at the exchange rate of N1,355.80 to the dollar. Justice Agbaza made the orders on Nov. 19, following the ex parte application and submissions by the claimant’s counsel, Emonye Adekwu, SAN, alongside Damilola Odesola, from Ade Okeaya-Inneh & Co. Law Firm. A certified true copy of the enrolled order by the court was obtained by the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Tuesday in Abuja. Iseghohi-Edwards, who carries on business as Edwards and Partners Law Firm, is seeking recovery of the money pursuant to an indemnity issued by the NGF. The claimant’s case is that the money belongs to him under an indemnity dated Dec. 20, 2018, issued by the NGF. The indemnity reportedly arose from an arrangement under which the Federal Government paid 100 million dollars to the NGF as a stakeholder. The money was to be held pending the determination of the Federal Government’s liability to Iseghohi-Edwards over legal and consultancy fees. The fees arose from services allegedly rendered in connection with the London and Paris Club loan transaction. Iseghohi-Edwards claimed he was retained by the Incorporated Trustees of the Association of Local Governments of Nigeria (ALGON) to represent the 774 local government councils in the London and Paris Clubs’ refund matters. He had instituted Suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/856/2016 against the Federal Government over the outstanding professional fees. According to his court filings, the Federal High Court, on Feb. 16, 2018, delivered judgment establishing the government’s indebtedness of 318 million dollars. The claimant said the government subsequently made a part-payment of 159 million dollars through promissory notes. He contended that the judgment fulfilled the condition contained in the NGF’s indemnity, thereby making the 100 million dollars payable directly to him. item.title: Orgs that leak data 'prioritize corporate interests over customers' says Have I Been Pwned’s Troy Hunt
item.description: Troy Hunt, the founder of data breach reporting site Have I Been Pwned (HIBP), has revealed how organizations respond when he informs them they’ve leaked data – if they respond at all. Hunt gave Anthropic’s Claude access to an email inbox containing over eight years of his email correspondence and then asked the AI to write a post summarising them, a method he said “was the best way to highlight the behaviors I keep seeing across many breaches and subsequent disclosure efforts.” Writing in person, Hunt described those behaviors as “standoffish behavior, deliberate delays, heavy involvement from lawyers, and a constant theme: prioritizing corporate interests over those of their customers.” Once Claude takes over writing duties, it opens with the observation that Hunt sent his standard notification email to 73 organizations between March 2018 and November 2026 and also used website contact forms. Claude/Hunt focuses on the breach notifications that don’t go well, for example when first contact “often goes nowhere” because “many organisations have no obvious way to report a security incident.” Some organizations Hunt contacted logged his notifications as customer support requests. “In one case, Troy received three automated surveys asking him to rate the support he'd received,” Claude wrote, before observing “A message that an organization’s customer data is being traded among criminals ended up in the same queue as a question about a late delivery.” Once someone at victim organization gets the message, a common response is to say they can find no evidence of the breach. Others try to play down the incident, saying it was only a website defacement or that Hunt is re-reporting a previous breach the victim has already disclosed. If an organization accepts Hunt is probably onto something, it typically says it needs to investigate the matter. Claude’s take on Hunt’s mails suggests he responds by pointing out that this is an irresponsible approach, because while the investigation takes place, “people whose data has been taken don't know they need to change a password or watch for phishing.” Next, victims send in the lawyers who ask if their employer or client is legally required to reveal the breach. Hunt typically replies by saying it is up to the victim to decide if the incident meets the threshold that triggers mandatory disclosure requirements under local laws, but that he intends to notify HIBP users regardless. Victims don’t like hearing that and respond in three ways: Calling to discuss disclosure, rather than committing to it; Asking to see the wording HIBP will use in its disclosure, a request that sees Hunt refer the victim to the HIBP site for examples of the thousand-plus breach reports already on the site; Arguing that disclosure, not the breach, is the real harm. Hunt/Claude suggests that each argument victims use to avoid disclosure “sounds reasonable on its own,” but argues “Together, they mean the people most affected by the breach are t

item.title: Eruption Extends Iwo Jima’s Beach
item.description: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Eruption Extends Iwo Jima’s… Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search October 26 November 11 NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison October 26 November 11 NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison October 26 November 11 Curtain Toggle 2-Up A volcanic eruption in the shallows near Iwo Jima has extended the Japanese island’s famed black sand beaches, at least temporarily. Signs of unrest began in late October 2026. On October 27, seismic sensors recorded a sharp uptick in activity, and Japan’s Meteorological Agency reported that the first photographs of the eruption were captured. Soon after, sensors on several satellites began to capture an array of observations. The OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 9 captured the left image on October 26, when the coast was still quiet. On November 11, Landsat 9 got its first clear view of the land the submarine volcano has built (right). A shortwave-infrared signature, a sign of the eruption’s heat, is shown in orange. A faint gray volcanic plume drifts southeast of the vent, and a streak of floating pumice stretches across the water in the same direction. A false-color backscatter radar image from the NISAR (NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar) satellite offered an even earlier look at the eruption. On October 28, despite heavy cloud cover, the radar detected a large disturbance in the water in the same area that erupted in December 2023. When the clouds cleared in early November, the MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) and VIIRS (Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite) sensors on NASA and NOAA satellites also captured signs of the ongoing eruption’s volcanic plumes and infrared signature . Japan’s Coast Guard released a report on November 16 confirming the formation of new land connected to the pre-existing beach. The eruption appears to have added roughly 50 hectares (125 acres) of new beach, about the area of 90 American football fields. That would enlarge the island by about 1.7 percent. The new land adjoins the southeast beach where American troops landed on February 19, 1945, beginning one of the bloodiest battles in the history of the U.S. Marines. The location of the eruption is no surprise to scientists. In addition to the 2023 eruption off the southeast coast, Iwo Jima had an eruption off its west coast in August 2025, said Daniel Slayback, a scientist at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center. How long the new land will persist remains an open question. New land created by the 2023 eruption succumbed to wave action after

item.title: Cisco and OpenAI pitch eBPF kernel plugins as the way to tame the patchpocalypse
item.description: Cisco and OpenAI have released an open-source tool called Shirudo to implement compensating controls in Linux, potentially improving security for users who can’t quickly patch newly discovered software flaws. Shirudo relies on eBPF, the technology that makes it possible to run sandboxed programs in the Linux kernel. eBPF programs are effectively kernel plug-ins but don’t get unrestricted access to system resources. Developers have mostly used eBPF to create network functions that enable things like the open source Kubernetes observability and security tool Cilium , a Cloud Native Computing Foundation project. Cisco and OpenAI think eBPF can help organizations cope with the flood of 100,000-plus software flaws reported this year, many after the debut of AI-powered bug finders. The increased volume of flaws, and patches to fix them, is a problem for many organizations which already struggle to test fixes or find change windows in which to implement them. That problem has seen greater interest in “compensating controls” – changes to applications or infrastructure that harden them against flaws or malware, without requiring a patch. With Shirudo, Cisco and OpenAI are suggesting two things: The privileges eBPF programs enjoy make them a fine way to implement compensating controls for Linux; Agents should scan your infrastructure for vulnerabilities, then use tools like OpenAI’s Codex to write compensating controls as eBPF programs at machine speed. “Shirudo” is apparently the Japanese word for “shield,” so Cisco and OpenAI have called the eBPF programs the tool creates “shields.” The two companies envision humans checking every shield Shirudo creates before putting it into production. Shirudo is open source and available here . The two companies say they’ve already demonstrated it could mitigate the recently discovered flaws in Java without requiring downtime for an Elasticsearch implementation. Cisco and OpenAI are not alone in advocating for compensating controls. Third-party software maintenance outfits like Rimini Street have used them for years to protect software when their clients no longer have the right to access patches. VMware has introduced “virtual patching.” Palo Alto Networks and Rapid 7 also like this approach, and offer automation to develop controls. Where Cisco and OpenAI differ is their decision to make Shirudo open source , and their ambition that other players adapt and advance it. That offer is not entirely altruistic, as if Shirudo takes off it could create more demand for Codex. Cisco’s angle comes from the fact it owns Isovalent, an early champion of eBPF and the creator of both Cilium and the Tetragon sub-project on which Shirudo is based. Switchzilla is using eBPF in other products, so normalizing its use through an open source project can’t hurt. ®

item.title: Anthropic says Claude solved an age-old math problem, but the written proof is 250,000 pages of slop
item.description: The leaders of the great model houses, Anthropic's Dario Amodei and OpenAI's Sam Altman, desperately want the world to believe AI is the skeleton key which will unlock the secrets of the universe. But if the AI can’t explain what it’s “proven,” are we actually any closer to understanding anything, or have we simply built another black box? That question is top of mind among mathematicians and computer scientists this week after Anthropic researcher Levent Alpöge claimed to have solved a mathematical conjecture so elusive it's gone unproven for more than 150 years. The fact that this note came out one day after Anthropic's record-setting IPO is a coincidence, we're sure. In a four-page post to his website, the researcher described how with the help of Claude, he believes he has proven the Riemann Hypothesis, one of seven Millennium problems so complex and so important that the Clay Mathematics Institute has offered a $1 million prize to anyone who is successful in solving them. The Riemann Hypothesis, conjectured by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann in 1859, contends that all nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function – those with a real part between zero and one – have a real part equal to 1/2. Confused? Don’t worry. We’ve linked to an explainer that goes into more detail here . What's important is that, if the Riemann Hypothesis is right, mathematicians can place tighter bounds on the difference between the actual distribution of prime numbers and mathematical estimates of that distribution. Researchers have previously attempted to disprove the conjecture through computational brute force, and therein have shown the hypothesis holds to at least 10 trillion zeros . There’s reason to believe that the Riemann Hypothesis is accurate, but the possibility remains that over a sufficiently long series the pattern might diverge. And so, more than 150 years after Riemann published his hypothesis, it has remained just that. Alpöge’s proof, if it can even be called that, is now the subject of great debate. The four pages in which Alpöge remarks on the discoveries he and Claude made aren’t exactly a proof, but rather 14 tarballs worth of Lean code totaling roughly 240 MB. Lean is an open source programming language commonly used to help validate mathematical proofs. The Clay Mathematics Institute, which oversees the seven Millennium Problems, has promoted the Riemann Hypothesis from “unsolved” to “active” status, but it is not yet considered solved. For Clay to consider the problem solved and award the prize, the proposed solution must be published in a qualifying outlet, remain available for scrutiny for at least two years, and receive broad acceptance from the mathematics community. As it stands, Alpöge describes the 250,000 pages of text generated by the model for its written proof as a “massive unreadable travesty of ‘slop.’” Not long after Alpöge's remarks and Lean code were published, Stanford mathematician Ravi Vakil released a nearly 1,000-pag

item.title: Will astronauts farm on the moon? Scientists successfully grow potatoes in simulated lunar dust
item.description:
Julian Dossett is a freelance writer living in Santa Fe, New Mexico. He primarily covers the rocket industry and space exploration and, in addition to science writing, contributes travel stories to New Mexico Magazine. In 2022 and 2024, his travel writing earned IRMA Awards. Previously, he worked as a staff writer at CNET. He graduated from Texas State University in San Marcos in 2011 with a B.A. in philosophy. He owns a large collection of sci-fi pulp magazines from the 1960s.

It's no secret that NASA is working towards a permanent presence on the moon. The space agency even plans to build a moon base for its astronauts to call home. But humans living inside lunar habitats around the clock will need three square meals a day, so researchers have been working on how to grow food on the moon. To that end, a team from the College of Agricultural Sciences at Oregon State University have been raising potatoes in simulated moon dust with promising results. The researchers published their findings Nov. 20 in the Microgravity science journal. "We found that potatoes can complete their entire life cycle in simulated lunar soil when supplemented with organic matter," Aymeric Goyer, associate professor at OSU's Department of Botany and Plant Pathology, said in a statement . "That's an important step toward developing reliable food production systems that could support long-term human exploration of the moon." To grow the spuds, the scientists used five different materials that are similar to regolith , the dust and rocks that cover the moon's surface. The moon contains various regions with unique surface makeups, so the materials they used simulated regolith from both lunar mare and lunar highland regions. The secret ingredient was vermicompost, a soil that's rich in nutrients. The team added different levels of vermicompost to the simulated regolith to grow the potatoes. They figured out that fake regolith mixed with 30 percent vermicompost worked about as well as growing potatoes with regular soil. Oregon State University researchers David Handy and Aymeric Goyer studying potatoes grown in lunar regolith. (Image credit: Aymeric Goyer/David Handy/OSU) "We believe the compost helps balance some of the toxicity we see in lunar regolith by reducing plant exposure to harmful compounds," David Handy, a postdoctoral researcher in Goyer's lab, said in the same statement. The idea is that astronauts in the future could bring a little nutrient-rich soil with them and mix it with regolith to grow potatoes. After all, it'd cost a ton to ship all that food from Earth. NASA funding supported this research.
